original.claim: Genetic influences accounted for an estimated 49.2% of variation in disordered-gambling liability in this twin sample.
original.method: Australian twins completed structured telephone interviews about gambling behavior, and biometric twin modeling estimated genetic and environmental contributions.
original.population: The sample comprised 4,764 Australian Twin Registry members aged 32 to 43 years; 57.2% were female.
original.outcome_measure: Lifetime DSM-IV pathological-gambling symptom counts assessed with the National Opinion Research Center DSM-IV Screen for Gambling Problems.

evidence.location: Abstract: Participants and Main Outcome Measure
evidence.quote: Four thousand seven hundred sixty-four individuals from 2889 twin pairs participated; twins were aged 32 to 43 years and 57% were women. Disordered gambling was defined based on lifetime DSM-IV pathological-gambling symptom counts.
The estimate of the proportion of variation in liability for disordered gambling due to genetic influences was 49.2%.
Twins were assessed through a structured telephone interview. Interviews were administered by trained lay interviewers who were blind to the status of the co-twin.

original.claim: Among non-Hispanic Black Iraq/Afghanistan-era veterans, APOE ε4 interacted with high combat exposure so that ε4 homozygotes had the highest PTSD rates and symptom severity.
original.method: The study assessed diagnoses through structured interview and modeled APOE ε4 by combat-exposure interactions separately in non-Hispanic White and Black veteran samples.
original.population: Participants were 765 non-Hispanic White and 859 non-Hispanic Black Iraq/Afghanistan-era veterans.
original.outcome_measure: Lifetime PTSD diagnosis and PTSD symptom severity measured with the Davidson Trauma Scale.

evidence.quote: Participants included 765 non-Hispanic White and 859 non-Hispanic Black Iraq/Afghanistan-era veterans. A structured interview established psychiatric diagnoses. Combat exposure and PTSD symptom severity were assessed via self-report.

Within the non-Hispanic Black sample, significant gene by environment interactions were observed for lifetime PTSD and PTSD symptom severity. When combat exposure was high, ε4 homozygotes exposed to high levels of combat reported the highest rates of PTSD and the worst symptom severity scores on the Davidson Trauma Scale.

original.claim: Maternal insensitivity predicted more preschool externalizing behavior only among children with the DRD4 7-repeat polymorphism; the combined-risk group's increase was sixfold.
original.method: Researchers videotaped mother-infant interaction, rated maternal sensitivity, genotyped DRD4 from cheek cells, and later collected mothers' Child Behavior Checklist reports.
original.population: The study observed 47 Dutch infants, including 23 boys, sampled through the Netherlands Twin Register.
original.outcome_measure: Externalizing behavior was the Child Behavior Checklist 2–3-year oppositional, aggressive, and overactive syndrome composite completed when children were 39 months old.

evidence.quote: Maternal insensitivity was associated with externalizing (oppositional, aggressive) behaviors, but only in the presence of the DRD4 7-repeat polymorphism. The increase in externalizing behaviors in children with the 7-repeat allele exposed to insensitive care compared to children without these combined risks was sixfold.

Mothers and infants were filmed during normal unstructured activities around the home and during two structured activities: feeding and free play. Mothers completed the Child Behavior Check List (CBCL/2–3 years) at 39 months. Cheek cells were collected at 50 months of age.
We observed 47 infants (23 males) at home at 10 months of age. All infants were sampled through the Netherlands Twin Register.

original.claim: No cumulative police-trauma index that weighted incident frequency and severity showed superior validity; weighting frequency by severity did not increase precision.
original.method: Police officers completed mailed self-report booklets that included the Critical Incident History Questionnaire, symptom measures, and ratings of incident frequency and severity.
original.population: The primary sample comprised 719 police officers from New York, Oakland, and San Jose; 79% were male and their mean age was 37 years.
original.outcome_measure: Cumulative Critical Incident History Questionnaire exposure indices, ratings of incident severity, and posttraumatic-stress symptoms.

evidence.quote: Because no index summarizing cumulative exposure to trauma had superior validity, our findings suggest that precision is not increased if frequency is weighted by severity.

The Critical Incident History Questionnaire indexes cumulative exposure to traumatic incidents in police by examining incident frequency and rated severity. All indices were only modestly related to posttraumatic stress disorder symptoms.

Police officers were recruited from the urban departments of New York, New York, and Oakland and San Jose, California. Participants giving informed consent completed a self-report questionnaire booklet including demographic, symptom, and other measures.
The primary sample comprised 719 officers (79% male), with a mean age of 37.0 years.

original.claim: Past and future time shifts produced spatial-compatibility effects only when participants moved to respond and only for larger shifts.
original.method: Undergraduates made sensibility judgments about past- or future-event sentences using toward or away responses either with movement or button pressing.
original.population: The final analyses included 79 right-handed undergraduates in the movement experiment and 76 in the no-movement experiment.
original.outcome_measure: Speed and accuracy of sensibility judgments under toward versus away response mappings.

evidence.quote: Participants read sentences involving past or future events and made sensibility judgment responses by moving toward or away from their body or by pressing the toward or away buttons without moving. Spatial compatibility effects were observed, but only when participants were moving to make their responses, and only for larger time shifts.

One hundred and seventy-seven undergraduate students participated. In the final analysis we excluded all but right-handed participants, leaving 79 participants in the Movement experiment and 76 in the No Movement experiment.

original.claim: In the social box-opening condition, infants preferred the puppet that helped an animate protagonist over the puppet that blocked it; 25 of 34 chose the helper.
original.method: Infants watched alternating puppet events in which an animate protagonist was helped to open a box or blocked, then chose between the helper and blocker; a matched inanimate-pincer control used the same physical actions.
original.population: Experiment 1 included 68 healthy full-term 5- and 9-month-old infants across social and inanimate-control conditions.
original.outcome_measure: The first puppet intentionally touched in the helper-versus-blocker choice test after habituation.

evidence.quote: The infant's choice was coded, by the blinded experimenter, as the first puppet the infant intentionally touched, that is, touched while concurrently looking at.

Sixteen 9-month-olds were assigned to the Social condition and 16 to the Inanimate Control condition. Eighteen 5-month-olds were assigned to the Social condition and 18 to the Inanimate Control condition.

In the Social condition, infants saw a plush animal hand puppet trying, with difficulty, to open the lid of a clear plastic box with a brightly colored rattle inside. The Protagonist was alternately aided by a prosocial puppet and thwarted by an antisocial puppet.
Infants in the Social condition significantly preferred the Opener over the Closer puppet (25 of 34 infants chose the Opener, binomial test, p < .01).

original.claim: Fifteen children showed a significant increase in full-scale IQ after relational-frame skills training, from a mean of 97 at baseline to 120 afterward.
original.method: In a within-participant school intervention, children completed computer-based training in Same, Opposite, More, and Less relations over 37 to 222 days, with IQ tested before and after training.
original.population: The first experiment enrolled an entire primary-school cohort of fifteen native-English-speaking 11- to 12-year-old children in Ireland.
original.outcome_measure: Full-scale IQ from the UK Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children, assessed before training and about one month after it ended.

evidence.quote: In Experiment 1, fifteen 11–12 year old children were exposed over several months to an intensive training intervention to improve their understanding of the relations Same, Opposite and More and Less.

Children were provided with a full IQ assessment approximately one month before commencing the training. The follow up IQ test was administered approximately one month following the completion of the training for each child.

evidence.location: p. 6, Results and discussion, Full scale IQ scores
evidence.quote: The average full scale IQ at baseline was in the average range at 97. At post-intervention full scale IQ was in the superior range at 120. This increase in full scale IQ from pre to post-intervention was significant, t(14) = 19.183, p < 0.001.

original.claim: Recognition memory for negative and positive emotional pictures exceeded memory for neutral pictures both 10 minutes and 20 hours after encoding, with the emotional-memory advantage larger at the later test.
original.method: Participants incidentally encoded negative, positive, and neutral pictures, then completed recognition tests after 10 minutes and 20 hours; corrected hit rates were analyzed by picture valence and retention interval.
original.population: The analyzed sample comprised 646 healthy young adults aged 18 to 36 years, including 464 women, after exclusions for incomplete data or below-chance performance.
original.outcome_measure: Corrected recognition hit rate, defined as hit rate minus false-alarm rate, for negative, positive, and neutral pictures at immediate and delayed tests.

evidence.quote: 44 participants were excluded due to incomplete data or below chance performance, resulting in a sample of n = 646 (464 females, age range 18-36 y, mean 24.4 y).

Participants incidentally encoded the mixed list of emotionally arousing and neutral pictures. 10 minutes later, participants completed an immediate recognition test. Recognition memory for the remaining pictures was tested again 20 hours later with the identical procedure.

evidence.location: p. 8, Results, Effects of emotional arousal on immediate and delayed memory performance
evidence.quote: A repeated-measures GLM with corrected hit rate (hit rate - false alarm rate) as dependent variable showed significant main effects as well as an interaction. Post hoc tests revealed emotional enhancement for negative and positive pictures in the immediate test and even more pronounced after 20 hours.

original.claim: A calculation-focused prompt reduced donations to an identifiable victim compared with a feeling-focused prompt, while it did not affect donations to statistical victims.
original.method: In a between-subjects campus experiment, participants completed either calculation or feeling prompts, read a charity request about an identifiable or statistical victim, and privately chose how much of five dollars to donate.
original.population: The fourth study recruited 165 students and other people on a university campus in Pennsylvania.
original.outcome_measure: The dollar amount, from the five one-dollar bills paid for participation, that participants sealed in an envelope as a charity donation.

evidence.quote: Students and other people on campus at a University in Pennsylvania (N = 165) were recruited. Each received a packet of questionnaires and received $5 in one dollar bills for participating.

In the calculation-priming condition, the questionnaire was entitled ‘Calculations Questionnaire.’ In the feeling-priming condition, the questionnaire instructed participants to base answers ‘on the feelings you experience.’ After completing the packet, participants received $5 in one dollar bills, an envelope, and a charity request; donating their earnings anonymously in the envelope was identical to the earlier studies.
When primed to calculate, participants donated significantly less to the identifiable victim then when primed to feel. However, priming had no effect on donations to statistical victims.

original.claim: Dark Triad traits were associated with less preventive behavior and more hoarding behavior during the COVID-19 pandemic.
original.method: A nationally representative Polish survey modeled Dark Triad and collective-narcissism associations with prevention and hoarding, including indirect paths through COVID-related health beliefs.
original.population: The study used a nationally representative sample of 755 people in Poland.
original.outcome_measure: Self-reported preventive and hoarding behaviors and coronavirus-related health-belief measures.

evidence.quote: In a nationally representative sample from Poland (N = 755), we examined relationships between the Dark Triad traits and collective narcissism and behaviors related to the COVID-19 pandemic, indirectly through health beliefs about the virus. We focused on preventive and hoarding behaviors.
Participants characterized by the Dark Triad traits engaged less in prevention and more in hoarding, whereas those characterized by collective narcissism engaged in more hoarding only.

original.claim: Among women in long-term relationships, higher average progesterone across the cycle was associated with lower facial-masculinity preference; daily estradiol and progesterone levels showed no general effect on that preference.
original.method: Women collected saliva daily across one menstrual cycle and attended three sessions in which they made forced choices between masculinized and feminized male faces; analyses modeled hormone levels and relationship status.
original.population: The study recruited women from Malopolska, Poland: 105 completed it, 102 provided daily saliva samples, and participants were 21 to 37 years old.
original.outcome_measure: At each session, participants selected the more attractive face from ten pairs of male faces manipulated to vary in facial masculinity.

evidence.quote: Women from the region of Malopolska in Poland were recruited. Out of 110 recruited participants 105 completed the study and 102 provided daily saliva samples collected throughout the entire menstrual cycle. Participants were between 21 and 37 years of age.
All women attended 3 meetings throughout the cycle. During each meeting women chose via 2-alternative forced choice participants from 10 pairs of male faces varying in masculinity.

In partnered women, with the increase in average progesterone levels masculinity preferences decreased. We did not find a general effect of daily P levels or daily E2 levels on facial-masculinity preference.

original.claim: Exposure alone produced 94% high end-state functioning for marked claustrophobic fear, compared with 45% when safety aids were available and 44% when they were used.
original.method: Participants with claustrophobic fear were randomly assigned to exposure alone, exposure with safety-aid availability, exposure with safety-aid use, placebo, or wait list and assessed before treatment, after treatment, and at follow-up.
original.population: The final sample was 72 University of Texas introductory-psychology students with marked claustrophobic fear; 86% were women and ages ranged from 18 to 49 years.
original.outcome_measure: High end-state functioning based on reliable pre-to-post change and subjective fear during a behavioral approach test in an enclosed chamber.

evidence.quote: High end-state functioning rates at posttreatment were as follows: EO 94%, SBA 45%, SBU 44%, PL 25%, and WL 0%. Findings suggest that it is the perception of the availability of safety aids as opposed to their actual use that exerts a disruptive effect on fear reduction.

Participants were classified as showing clinically significant change if their level of pre- to posttreatment BAT 1 fear change was statistically reliable and if their level of functioning at posttreatment, as measured by their subjective fear during BAT 1, fell outside the range of the claustrophobic population.

The final sample (N = 72) consisted primarily of women (86%), ranging in age from 18 to 49 years. Eligible participants were randomly assigned to one of five conditions: EO, exposure with SBU, exposure with SBA, credible psychological PL, or WL control.

original.claim: Participants reported greater happiness and life satisfaction while in a good than a bad mood, and attributing bad mood to a transient external source eliminated its negative impact on those judgments.
original.method: In one experiment students wrote vividly about a recent happy or sad event while receiving different explanations for room-induced feelings, then rated well-being and current mood.
original.population: Experiment 1 used 61 introductory psychology students randomly assigned to experimental conditions and run in groups of three or four.
original.outcome_measure: Ratings of happiness and satisfaction with life as a whole, alongside ratings of current happiness and feeling good or bad.

evidence.quote: In both experiments, subjects reported more happiness and satisfaction with their life as a whole when in a good mood than when in a bad mood. However, the negative impact of bad moods was eliminated when subjects were induced to attribute their present feelings to transient external sources.

The questions included two measures of general well-being. One of these pertained to general happiness and the other to life satisfaction. Following these measures, subjects' present affective states were assessed.

Participants were asked to describe as vividly and in as much detail as possible a recent event that made them feel really good or one that made them feel really bad. Following these descriptions, participants were asked to answer general questions.
Sixty-one introductory psychology students who were randomly assigned to experimental conditions received course credit for their participation. They were run in groups of three or four persons each.

original.claim: Undergraduates judged sexual-availability tactics most effective for women seeking short-term mates, resource-potential tactics most effective for men seeking long-term mates, and immediate resource-giving most effective for men seeking short-term mates.
original.method: Separate groups of undergraduates judged the effectiveness of self-promotion and competitor-derogation mate-attraction tactics as a function of the actor's sex and short- versus long-term mating context.
original.population: The studies used separate groups of undergraduate participants.
original.outcome_measure: Participants' judgments of the perceived effectiveness of specified mate-attraction tactics.

evidence.quote: In Studies 1 and 2, separate groups of undergraduate participants judged sexual availability tactics as most effective when used by women seeking short-term mates. Showing resource potential was judged most effective for men seeking a long-term mate, whereas giving resources immediately was judged most effective for men seeking short-term mates.
In this article, 7 evolutionary hypotheses about the context-specific nature of mate attraction effectiveness were empirically tested and supported.

original.claim: A single computerized attention-modification session changed threat-attention bias in people selected for social-anxiety symptoms.
original.method: Participants were randomly assigned, under participant and research-assistant blinding, to attention-modification or attention-control computer training, with bias measured before and after training.
original.population: Ninety-four undergraduate-pool participants recruited for difficulty giving speeches and screened for elevated Liebowitz Social Anxiety Scale scores.
original.outcome_measure: Attention-bias indices from the Attention Bias Assessment Task, measured before and after the computer task.

evidence.quote: Participants in the AMP group showed significantly less attention bias to threat after training and lower levels of anxiety in response to a public-speaking challenge than did the participants in the Attention Control Condition (ACC) group.

Participants comprised 94 individuals recruited from an undergraduate pool with an advertisement for individuals with difficulty giving speeches. Participants were screened on the basis of their Liebowitz Social Anxiety Scale score and invited to participate if they scored greater than 26.

Participants were randomly assigned to either the AMP or the ACC. The participants and the research assistants working with the participants were blind to the participants’ condition. Participants then completed the Attention Bias Assessment Task, which provided a baseline index of attention bias. Participants then completed the attention training task.
The AMP group was significantly faster in its response latency to invalid social threat words than the ACC group at posttraining.

original.claim: M170 face-response strength was modulated by fearful versus neutral valence only when participants could reliably detect the briefly masked fearful faces; better detection was also associated with higher trait anxiety.
original.method: Healthy volunteers underwent magnetoencephalography while viewing briefly presented fearful, happy, or neutral target faces followed by neutral masks, making fear-detection and confidence button responses.
original.population: Thirty-one healthy volunteers, including 17 women, with a mean age of 28.9 years participated; eight also completed a trait-anxiety inventory.
original.outcome_measure: M170 magnetoencephalography response to masked fearful versus neutral faces, individual fear-detection sensitivity from receiver-operating-characteristic analysis, and trait-anxiety scores.

evidence.quote: The strength of the M170 response was modulated by valence only when subjects could reliably detect the masked fearful faces. Subjects who were better able to detect fearful faces also showed higher trait anxiety levels.
Thirty-one normal volunteers (17 women) aged 28.9 (mean) ± 5.8 years participated in the study. Eight of the 31 subjects also completed a State–Trait Anxiety Inventory.

evidence.location: Method: Trial Structure and Behavioral Data Analysis
evidence.quote: Each pair of faces consisted of a fearful, happy or neutral target face that was immediately followed by a neutral face, which served as a mask. Subjects indicated fear or no fear with a button press and rated confidence. Sensitivity to fearful stimuli was determined using A′, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve.

original.claim: Guided self-help cognitive-behavioral therapy produced higher 12-month binge-eating abstinence than treatment as usual.
original.method: Individuals with recurrent binge eating were randomized in a health-maintenance-organization setting to eight sessions of manual-based guided self-help cognitive-behavioral therapy or treatment as usual.
original.population: One hundred twenty-three individuals with recurrent binge eating were randomized; mean age was 37.2 years and 91.9% were female.
original.outcome_measure: Binge-eating abstinence measured with the Eating Disorder Examination, plus questionnaire measures of eating concerns, depression, and social adjustment.

evidence.quote: One hundred twenty-three individuals were randomized. The study evaluated a manual-based guided self-help form of cognitive-behavioral therapy, delivered in 8 sessions in a Health Maintenance Organization setting over a 12-week period, compared with treatment as usual.

At 12-month follow-up, guided self-help cognitive-behavioral therapy resulted in greater abstinence from binge eating (64.2%) than treatment as usual (44.6%), as measured by the Eating Disorder Examination.

original.claim: Greater chronic loneliness was associated with greater self-reported physical warmth extracted through bathing.
original.method: Undergraduates completed lifestyle and bathing-habit questionnaires plus a loneliness scale in a cross-sectional survey.
original.population: Fifty-one undergraduates recruited outside a university dining hall participated for two dollars.
original.outcome_measure: A composite of bath or shower frequency, duration, and preferred water temperature, alongside the UCLA Loneliness Scale.

evidence.quote: We hypothesized that chronic or trait loneliness of our participants would be positively associated with the frequency, duration, and preferred water temperature of the showers and baths that they take.

Participants completed two surveys in a random order, including three key items about their bathing habits: how often they usually take a bath, what temperature water they use, and how much time they spend in the bath. Next, participants filled out the short version of the UCLA Loneliness scale.
Fifty-one undergraduates (26 females, and 25 males) were recruited for the study outside of their commons dining hall in exchange for $2.

The physical warmth extraction index variable correlated r=.57, p=.0001, with UCLA Loneliness scores, such that 32.5% of the variation in physical warmth extraction during bathing was explained by how lonely the participant was.

original.claim: Auditory verbal labels produced faster and more accurate verification of congruent objects than characteristic nonverbal sounds.
original.method: University undergraduates heard a verbal label or nonverbal sound, then made match or mismatch judgments about a picture across within-subject verification trials.
original.population: Forty-three University of Pennsylvania undergraduates participated across Experiments 1A–1C for course credit.
original.outcome_measure: Correct-trial picture-verification reaction time and accuracy.

evidence.quote: Verbal cues, such as the word “cat,” lead to faster and more accurate verification of congruent objects and rejection of incongruent objects than do either nonverbal cues, such as the sound of a cat meowing.
A total of 43 University of Pennsylvania undergraduates volunteered in the experiments in exchange for course credit: 18 in Experiment 1A, 15 in Experiment 1B, and 10 in Experiment 1C.

On each trial, participants heard a cue—a verbal label or a nonverbal sound—followed by a picture. The picture matched the cue 50% of the time. Participants responded by pressing a match or does not match key on a keyboard.

original.claim: Participants who traced fluid rather than nonfluid line drawings generated more and more original uses for a newspaper, and fluid movement also improved remote-association performance but not GRE math performance.
original.method: Across experiments, undergraduates were randomly assigned to trace fluid or nonfluid drawings before completing creative-use, category-flexibility, remote-association, or GRE tasks.
original.population: Experiment 1 included 30 undergraduates, 63% women; Experiment 3 included 150 undergraduates, 54% men.
original.outcome_measure: Number and independent-judge originality ratings of creative newspaper uses, plus correct Remote Associates Test triads and GRE math problems.

evidence.quote: Across 3 experiments, fluid arm movement led to enhanced creativity in 3 domains: creative generation, cognitive flexibility, and remote associations.

Thirty undergraduates (63% women) participated and traced either the three fluid or the three nonfluid drawings, based on random assignment. Subsequently, participants generated as many creative uses for a newspaper as possible within 1 min. Participants who made fluid movements demonstrated greater fluency and originality than did those who made nonfluid movements.
Participants who made fluid movements solved more RAT triads than did those who made nonfluid movements, but they did not solve a different number of GRE math problems.

original.claim: Children assigned to immediate Bounce Back showed greater three-month improvement in posttraumatic-stress and anxiety symptoms than children assigned to delayed intervention.
original.method: School clinicians delivered a 10-session cognitive-behavioral group program to children randomized to immediate treatment or a three-month waitlist.
original.population: Seventy-four school children in grades 1 through 5 with clinically significant posttraumatic-stress symptoms participated with their primary caregivers.
original.outcome_measure: Parent- and child-reported posttraumatic stress and depression, plus child-reported anxiety symptoms.

evidence.quote: Parent- and child-report of posttraumatic stress and depression, and child report of anxiety symptoms, were assessed at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months.

Participants were 74 school children (grades 1-5) and their primary caregivers. All participating students endorsed clinically significant posttraumatic stress symptoms. School clinicians were trained to deliver Bounce Back, a 10-session cognitive-behavioral group intervention. Children were randomized to Immediate or Delayed (3-month waitlist) Intervention.

Compared to children in the Delayed condition, children who received Bounce Back immediately demonstrated significantly greater improvements in parent- and child-reported posttraumatic stress and child-reported anxiety symptoms over the 3-month intervention.

original.claim: Students paid one dollar to tell another student that a boring task was enjoyable rated the task more enjoyable than both unpaid controls and students paid twenty dollars.
original.method: After completing repetitive peg-and-spool tasks, male students were assigned to a control condition or paid one or twenty dollars to describe the task positively to a waiting student, then gave blinded interview ratings.
original.population: The experiment recruited 71 male students from Stanford University's introductory psychology course; data from 11 were discarded before the reported condition means.
original.outcome_measure: Interview rating of how interesting and enjoyable the tasks were on an 11-point scale from extremely dull and boring to extremely interesting and enjoyable.

evidence.quote: Would you rate how you feel about them on a scale from −5 to +5 where −5 means they were extremely dull and boring, +5 means they were extremely interesting and enjoyable, and zero means they were neutral.

These subjects were hired for one dollar to tell a waiting subject that tasks, which were really rather dull and boring, were interesting, enjoyable, and lots of fun. Average ratings for how enjoyable tasks were were −.45 for Control, +1.35 for One Dollar, and −.05 for Twenty Dollars.
Seventy-one male students in the introductory psychology course at Stanford University were used in the experiment. Three conditions were run, Control, One Dollar, and Twenty Dollars.

original.claim: Women veterans reporting military sexual trauma had higher odds of meeting eating-disorder criteria, whereas combat exposure was not associated with eating disorders.
original.method: A mail-based cross-sectional survey used logistic regression to predict eating-disorder status from military sexual trauma and combat exposure while adjusting for demographic variables.
original.population: Four hundred seven women veterans aged 18 to 70 years using urban VA medical-center services returned the survey.
original.outcome_measure: Probable anorexia or bulimia based on the SCOFF and binge-eating disorder based on the Eating Disorder Examination-Questionnaire.

evidence.quote: Participants were women age 18–70 using VA medical center services (N = 407). We estimated a cross-sectional logistic regression model to predict eating disorders as a function of military sexual trauma and combat exposure, adjusting for demographic variables. Women reporting military sexual trauma had twice the odds of an eating disorder compared to women who did not. Combat exposure was not associated with eating disorders.

To assess anorexia and bulimia, we used the SCOFF Clinical Prediction Guide, a 5-item measure of core eating disorder symptoms. To assess binge eating disorder, we used the Eating Disorder Examination-Questionnaire. Both measures were self-report.

original.claim: In the first causal-learning experiment, the superlearning cue received higher causal ratings than its control cue.
original.method: Undergraduates completed computer-based human causal-learning blocks using food cues and graded allergic-reaction outcomes.
original.population: Fifteen undergraduate volunteers at the Health Sciences University of Hokkaido participated in Experiment 1.
original.outcome_measure: Keyboard-entered ratings of the causal strength of food cues for allergic reactions.

evidence.quote: We conducted four experiments to investigate causal superlearning, a phenomenon in human causal learning analogous to superconditioning. Experiment 1 demonstrated superlearning relative to appropriate control conditions.

evidence.location: Experiment 1: Participants and Apparatus and stimuli
evidence.quote: The participants were 15 undergraduate students from the Health Sciences University of Hokkaido. Participants entered their Yes/No responses and their ratings by means of a keyboard. Four different outcomes, strong, moderate, weak, and no allergic reactions, were used.

original.claim: Participants bid less for reward-associated shapes paired with stop signals than for comparable shapes not paired with stop signals.
original.method: The experiments combined reward learning with a stop-signal phase that paired some shapes with stopping, followed by an auction valuation phase.
original.population: Experiment 1 analyzed 32 UC San Diego participants after four exclusions; their mean age was 21.5 years and 22 were female.
original.outcome_measure: Willingness-to-pay bids for abstract shapes in the auction phase.

evidence.quote: We developed a novel paradigm with three consecutive phases: implicit reward learning, a stop-signal task, and an auction procedure. In two experiments, we found that participants bid less for shapes that were paired with stop-signals compared to shapes that were not.

Thirty-six participants at UCSD provided written informed consent. Three participants were excluded for not understanding the auction-phase. One participant was also excluded when we discovered he had been informed about the objective of the experiment prior to participation, leaving N = 32 (mean age = 21.5y; 22 female).

original.claim: Abrupt violations, but not the emergence of regularity, trigger phasic pupil dilation during rapid sound sequences when those changes are task-irrelevant.
original.method: Listeners heard rapid tone-pip sequences containing abrupt structural violations or emergent regularities while pupil size was recorded across multiple experiments.
original.population: Experiment 1A included 18 listeners and 1B included 14; later experiments used samples from 12 to 30 listeners.
original.outcome_measure: Phasic pupil-dilation responses to transitions in tone-pip sequences.

evidence.quote: We used rapid tone-pip sequences that contained salient pattern-changes associated with abrupt structural violations vs. emergence of regular structure. Phasic pupil dilations (PDR) were monitored ... only abrupt structural violations evoke a PDR.
Exp1A (n = 18) ... Experiment 1B (n = 14) ... Experiment 4A (n = 12) ... combined groups (n = 30).

original.claim: Non-deceptive placebos reduce self-reported emotional distress and the late positive potential during negative-picture viewing.
original.method: Across two experiments, participants were randomly assigned to a non-deceptive placebo or control condition before viewing highly arousing negative pictures.
original.population: Experiment 1 had 68 participants and Experiment 2 had 218 participants.
original.outcome_measure: Self-reported emotional distress and the late positive potential measured during picture viewing.

evidence.quote: Across two experiments that during a highly arousing negative picture viewing task, non-deceptive placebos reduce both a self-report and neural measure of emotional distress, the late positive potential.

In Experiment 1 (n = 68) ... Experiment 2 (n = 218), using a similar image viewing paradigm. In both experiments, we randomly assigned participants to the non-deceptive placebo group or a control group.

original.claim: Higher collective risk strengthens cooperative social norms, which promote cooperation and remain more resistant when risk changes.
original.method: Participants completed a 30-day online collective-risk social-dilemma experiment with repeated contributions, norm expectations, and a final punishment phase.
original.population: 286 participants began the 30-day online experiment; repeated-measures analyses report 283 individuals.
original.outcome_measure: Contributions, empirical and normative expectations, punishment behavior, and responses to changes in collective risk.

evidence.quote: Using a 30-day collective-risk social dilemma experiment to measure norm change in a controlled setting ... higher risk leads to stronger social norms that are more resistant to erosion when the risk changes.
30-day online experiment (n = 286) ... n = 283 individuals repeatedly measured during the experiment.

original.claim: Listeners classified as high spontaneous speech synchronizers showed an advantage on a phonological word-learning task.
original.method: A new cohort completed a spontaneous speech-synchronization test and then listened to continuous pseudo-word streams before a segmentation test.
original.population: Forty-four native English-speaking participants, aged 19 to 31 years, completed the synchronization and word-learning tasks.
original.outcome_measure: Phase-locking values from the synchronization task and accuracy in segmenting tri-syllabic pseudo-words during the word-learning test.

evidence.quote: A second cohort of 44 individuals (11 males; mean age, 21; age range, 19 to 31) completed the SSS-test and the word-learning task. All participants were native English speakers with self-reported normal hearing and no neurological deficits.

evidence.location: Spontaneous Speech Synchronization test predicts word learning
evidence.quote: A new sample of participants (N = 44) was recruited to complete the SSS-test as well as a word-form learning task. Participants listened for two minutes to a continuous repetition of four tri-syllabic pseudo-words, which were randomly concatenated without silence gaps between them. Next, they completed a testing phase to assess whether they correctly segmented the pseudo-words.

evidence.location: Spontaneous Speech Synchronization test predicts word learning
evidence.quote: By splitting this new population into high and low synchronizers, we find that high synchronizers have a significant learning advantage in the phonological word-learning task.

original.claim: Having a choice over upcoming negative images reduced negative experience, skin conductance, and respiratory reactivity while increasing expressivity and cardiovascular reactivity; choice generally reinforced calming effects for positive images.
original.method: In a within-subject design, participants viewed positive and negative images they selected themselves or the exact same images imposed without choice.
original.population: Sixty-five university participants took part: 33 men and 32 women, aged 18.8 to 44.6 years.
original.outcome_measure: Outcomes were self-reported emotional experience, skin conductance, respiratory and cardiovascular reactivity, and facial expressivity while viewing the images.

evidence.quote: Results show that having the choice in negative contexts decreased negative experience, skin conductance, and respiration reactivity, while enhancing expressivity and cardiovascular reactivity. In positive contexts, choosing generally reinforced the image calming effect.

In a within-subject design, we compared emotional responses of 65 participants when they viewed negative and positive images they could select (use of Situation selection) vs. when they were imposed the exact same images (Situation selection not used).
Participants’ ages ranged between 18.8 and 44.6 years, with a mean of 21.8 years (SD = 3.4 years).

Sixty-five participants thus fully participated in our study (33 males and 32 females). Participants were either first year Psychology students participating for course credits (N = 45), or other discipline first year students participating for the equivalent of USD50 (N = 20).

Expressivity was assessed using bipolar surface EMG electrodes were standard 4 mm Ag-AgCl sensors. Left Corrugator Supercilii, left Zygomaticus Major, and left Orbicularis Oculi were the three targeted regions.

Participants used a rating slider for continuously reporting their emotion experience (Variable Assessment Transducer, Biopac Systems, Inc., Goleta, CA, USA) over the full duration of the picture presentations.

original.claim: People's estimates of a fragmented triangle's missing corner and angle show scale-dependent deviations from Euclidean geometry.
original.method: Adults completed triangle-completion, missing-angle, and categorical-reasoning tasks with triangles that varied greatly in size and shape.
original.population: Educated U.S. adults: 40 in Experiment 1, 100 in Experiment 2, 29 in Experiment 3, 65 in Experiment 4, and 407 in Experiment 5.
original.outcome_measure: Estimated location and angle of a triangle's missing corner, response times, and categorical judgments of size and shape.

evidence.quote: An analysis of the distribution of participants’ errors in localizing a fragmented triangle’s missing corner reveals scale-dependent deviations from a deterministic Euclidean representation of planar triangles.
In Experiment 1, we asked educated U.S. adults (N = 40) ... Experiment 2 ... Amazon Mechanical Turk (N = 100) ... Experiment 4 (N = 65) ... Experiment 5 ... Amazon Mechanical Turk (N = 407).

original.claim: At four degrees from fixation, accuracy declined least for positive facial valence and most for negative facial valence, without a speed-accuracy trade-off or response bias explanation.
original.method: Adults judged happy, fearful, and neutral face valence at locations across the parafovea while their eye position was tracked.
original.population: Fifty-eight adults were recruited; after exclusions, 56 adults aged 18 to 37 years were included in analysis.
original.outcome_measure: The outcomes were accuracy and response measures for facial-valence judgments at different eccentricities, with eye tracking used to monitor fixation.

evidence.quote: Participants (n = 58) judged the valence of emotional faces across the parafovea (≤ 4°, positive, negative, or neutral) while their eyes were being tracked.

Positive valence perception was least affected by eccentricity (accuracy reduction of 10–19% at 4°) and negative the most (accuracy reduction of 35–38% at 4°), and this was not a result of speed-accuracy trade-off or response biases.
After excluding two participants from the block-design experiment, 56 participants aged 18–37 years were included in the analysis.

original.claim: AI chatbots produced more creative alternate-use responses than humans on average, but the best human ideas matched or exceeded the chatbots' best ideas.
original.method: Researchers compared 256 human participants and three AI chatbots on the Alternate Uses Task, asking for uncommon and creative uses for everyday objects.
original.population: The human sample comprised 256 Prolific participants who passed attention checks; the comparison included three current AI chatbots.
original.outcome_measure: Outcomes were Alternate Uses Task response creativity, including semantic-distance scores and creativity ratings by blinded human raters.

evidence.quote: On average, the AI chatbots outperformed human participants. While human responses included poor-quality ideas, the chatbots generally produced more creative responses. However, the best human ideas still matched or exceed those of the chatbots.

In this study, we compared the creativity of humans (n = 256) with that of three current AI chatbots using the alternate uses task (AUT), which is the most used divergent thinking task. Participants were asked to generate uncommon and creative uses for everyday objects.
Native English speakers were recruited via the online platform Prolific (www.prolific.co) and paid 2£ for the about 13-min participation.

Of the 279 participants with full data, 256 passed the attention checks (108 females, 145 males, 2 other, and 1 preferred not to identify the gender identity) and their results were included in the present study.

On average, the AI chatbots outperformed the human participants in both mean scores (all responses to an object averaged) and max scores (the best response to an object). This advantage was observed for both the semantic distance of the responses and the subjective ratings of creativity provided by unbiased human raters who were unaware of that some of the responses were generated by AI.
Additionally, human raters who were blind to the presence of AI-generated responses evaluated the responses.

original.claim: Across 45 countries, a higher Google-search future-orientation index was strongly associated with higher per-capita GDP.
original.method: Researchers compared 2010 Google Trends searches for the following versus previous calendar year with national purchasing-power-parity GDP data.
original.population: The analysis included 45 countries with Google Trends and CIA World Factbook data and at least five million Internet users.
original.outcome_measure: The future-orientation index was the ratio of searches for the coming year to searches for the previous year, compared with per-capita GDP.

evidence.quote: We compute the future orientation index for each of 45 countries with data from the search engine Google for users located in the country in question from the year 2010, using the search terms “2009” and “2011”.

We compare the future orientation index to the country's per capita GDP, calculated on a purchasing power parity basis, which we retrieve from the CIA World Factbook which provides figures as of 1 July 2010. Our analysis considers countries for which both Google Trends and the CIA World Factbook provide data and to reduce noise excludes countries with fewer than five million Internet users, for which few search data are available.

We uncover a strong tendency for countries in which Google users enquire more about the future to exhibit a larger per capita GDP (Fig. 1b; Pearson correlation coefficient r = 0.78, df = 43, p < 0.001).

original.claim: Six-month-old infants followed a model's gaze in attention-grabbing contexts whether or not the model first supplied ostensive communicative cues.
original.method: Infants viewed actor gaze-shift videos while a remote eye tracker recorded their gaze direction across trial blocks.
original.population: Twenty-two six-month-old infants, including 14 girls, were analyzed.
original.outcome_measure: Eye-tracked infant gaze following after a model shifted gaze toward an object.

evidence.quote: We demonstrate that 6-month-old infants follow others' gaze direction in situations that are highly attention-grabbing. This occurs irrespective of whether these situations include communicative intent and ostensive cues or not.
Twenty-two six-month-olds participated in the experiment. Infants were seated on their parent's lap approximately 60 cm from the screen of a Tobii T120 remote eye tracker. Gaze was recorded at 60 Hz.

original.claim: In controlled crossover trading studies, cortisol and testosterone administration shifted investment toward riskier assets.
original.method: Healthy young men completed a computerized trading simulator after hormone and placebo conditions in double-blind, placebo-controlled balanced crossover studies.
original.population: The usable samples were 29 healthy men in the cortisol study and 36 healthy men in the testosterone study, aged 18 to 30 years.
original.outcome_measure: Amounts invested in high- versus low-variance simulated stocks across 80 trading trials.

evidence.quote: We found that both cortisol and testosterone shifted investment towards riskier assets.

evidence.location: Cortisol and testosterone administration studies: Subjects
evidence.quote: A total of 34 healthy men aged 18–30 were recruited to take part in the cortisol study, resulting in a sample size of 29 subjects. Forty-one healthy men aged 18–30 were recruited for the testosterone study, resulting in a total usable sample size of 36.

evidence.location: Effects of administered cortisol or testosterone on male preferences for high volatility assets
evidence.quote: Healthy young male volunteers took part in a computerized trading simulator after being administered either cortisol or testosterone using a double-blind placebo-controlled balanced crossover design. Each subject was tested twice, once following hormone treatment and once following placebo.

evidence.location: Effects of administered cortisol or testosterone on male preferences for high volatility assets
evidence.quote: Subjects were shown plots of the price sequence for two stocks and had to decide how much to invest in each over a total of 80 trials. In any given trial, a stock could be in a high or low variance-return state.

original.claim: Professional musicians showed no significant McGurk effect for any tested phoneme, whereas non-musician controls showed the illusion for several phonemes.
original.method: Musicians and non-musician controls completed syllable-recognition trials with congruent and incongruent audiovisual speech stimuli and unimodal control trials.
original.population: Eighty healthy age-matched graduate students participated: 40 music-conservatory musicians with at least eight years of training and 40 non-musician university students.
original.outcome_measure: The outcome was syllable-recognition responses to audiovisual and unimodal presentations of eight spoken phonemes, including McGurk-illusion responses.

evidence.quote: 80 healthy age-matched graduate students volunteered to the study. 40 were musicians of Brescia Luca Marenzio Conservatory of Music with at least 8–13 years of musical academic studies.

40 University students (24 females, 16 males) aging on average 23 took part to the study. Participants were recruited through Sona System (a system for recruiting students who earn credit for their academic courses by participating in research studies). Their inclusion depended on their lack of musical studies and specific interest in music as a hobby. None of them played a musical instrument or used to listen to music for more than 1 hour per day, as ascertained by a specific questionnaire.

Overall musicians showed no significant McGurk effect for any of the phonemes. Controls showed a marked McGurk effect for several phonemes (including alveolar-nasal, velar-occlusive and bilabial ones).

/la/, /da/, /ta/, /ga/, /ka/, /na/, /ba/, /pa/ phonemes were presented to participants in audiovisual congruent and incongruent conditions, or in unimodal (only visual or only auditory) conditions while engaged in syllable recognition tasks.

original.claim: Garden-pea seedlings use a fan cue paired with light to guide their growth direction, overriding their usual phototropism.
original.method: Pea seedlings trained in Y-mazes experienced fan and light on the same or opposite arm for three days; a test group then received fan alone and growth arm was recorded.
original.population: Garden-pea seedlings; 26 were in the fan-only test group and 19 in the control group.
original.outcome_measure: The arm of the Y-maze into which each seedling grew after training and testing.

evidence.quote: By using a Y-maze task, we show that the position of a neutral cue, predicting the location of a light source, affected the direction of plant growth. This learned behaviour prevailed over innate phototropism.

Before the testing day, the seedlings were further subdivided randomly into a test group (n = 26) and a control group (n = 19) ... On the morning after the testing day, we visually inspected the seedlings and recorded the arm of the maze they had grown into.

original.claim: Arousing emotional information is remembered through an amygdala-hippocampal route, whereas valenced but nonarousing information depends on controlled prefrontal-hippocampal encoding.
original.method: The study combined functional MRI and behavioral memory studies, including a divided-attention manipulation while participants encoded emotional words.
original.population: 28 young adults in the functional-MRI study and 24 participants in the behavioral divided-attention study.
original.outcome_measure: Memory enhancement for arousing and valenced nonarousing words, plus neural activity during encoding.

evidence.quote: A behavioral companion study, with a divided-attention paradigm, confirmed that memory enhancement for valenced, nonarousing words relied on controlled encoding processes: concurrent task performance reduced the enhancement effect.

By using functional MRI and behavioral studies, we found that distinct cognitive and neural processes contribute to emotional memory enhancement for arousing information versus valenced, nonarousing information. The former depended on an amygdalar-hippocampal network, whereas the latter was supported by a prefrontal cortex-hippocampal network implicated in controlled encoding processes.

To test this hypothesis, 24 participants (12 women and 12 men) encoded words used in the functional MRI experiment while performing a hard auditory discrimination task, performing an easy auditory discrimination task, or performing no secondary task.

Participants comprised 28 young adults (14 women and 14 men) who were scanned on a Siemens Allegra 3 Tesla head-only MRI scanner while they encoded words that were neutral, negative and nonarousing, or negative and arousing.

original.claim: Conscious visual perception is associated with activity in the mid-dorsolateral prefrontal cortex when discrimination performance is matched.
original.method: A behavioral study and a functional-MRI study used metacontrast masking to vary subjective consciousness while matching objective visual discrimination.
original.population: Eight people completed the behavioral study; 14 volunteers entered the fMRI study and 13 were analyzed.
original.outcome_measure: Subjective consciousness reports, objective visual-target discrimination, and fMRI activity.

evidence.quote: By using a paradigm based on metacontrast masking, we created experimental conditions in which the subjective report of consciousness differs but the objectively measured ability to discriminate visual targets does not. ... A comparison of the neural activity associated with these conditions as measured by functional MRI showed that conscious perception is associated with spatially specific activity in the mid-dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (area 46).

Eight people participated in this study. After the presentation of the target and the mask, the participants were first asked to decide whether a diamond or a square was presented. Then they had to indicate whether they actually saw the target or whether they simply guessed the answer.
Fourteen volunteers participated in this experiment. The data for one participant were discarded because of unsatisfactory behavioral performance.

original.claim: Across four experiments, adaptive dual n-back training produced larger pre-to-post gains in fluid-intelligence test scores than no-training controls, with gains increasing with training duration.
original.method: Healthy young adults completed four pretest-posttest experiments in which matched groups either received adaptive dual n-back working-memory training for 8 to 19 days or received no training.
original.population: The study recruited 70 healthy young University of Bern community participants; after one training participant did not complete sessions, analyses included 34 trained and 35 control participants.
original.outcome_measure: Fluid-intelligence performance was the number of correct responses in 10 minutes on visual-analogy matrix tests: Raven's Advanced Progressive Matrices or the Bochumer Matrizen-Test.

evidence.location: Materials and Methods: Participants and Procedure
evidence.quote: For this study, we conducted four individual experiments involving a total of 70 healthy young participants (36 female; mean age, 25.6 years of age; SD, 3.3) recruited from the University of Bern community, 35 of whom performed working-memory training in four different training settings (one of the participants failed to complete the required training sessions and was thus discarded from the data analysis, resulting in a final N of 34). These training groups were matched to four control groups who did not have training (n = 35).

evidence.location: Materials and Methods: Participants and Procedure
evidence.quote: The crucial difference among the four training settings was the number of training sessions between pre- and posttests, ranging from 8 to 19 sessions, with the control groups receiving the pre- and posttesting at the same intervals as the trained groups.

We used standardized fluid intelligence tests consisting of visual analogy problems of increasing difficulty. For the eight-session experiment we used Raven's Advanced Progressive Matrices; for the others we used the Bochumer Matrizen-Test. The number of correct solutions in 10 minutes served as the dependent variable.

The improvement in the groups that received the apparent benefit of training was substantially superior, which was confirmed by the significant group × test-session interaction. Transfer to fluid intelligence varied as a function of training time.

original.claim: By the end of the school year, higher female teachers' math anxiety was associated with lower girls', but not boys', math achievement, and girls' traditional gender-ability beliefs statistically mediated that association.
original.method: Researchers measured math anxiety in first- and second-grade female teachers and assessed their students' mathematics achievement and gender-ability beliefs near the beginning and end of the school year.
original.population: The study included 17 first- and second-grade female teachers from a large Midwestern urban school district and 117 students: 65 girls and 52 boys.
original.outcome_measure: Teacher anxiety was measured with the 25-item short Mathematics Anxiety Rating Scale; student outcomes were Woodcock-Johnson III Applied Problems scores and a drawing-based gender-ability-belief measure.

evidence.location: Introduction and Methods: Teachers and Students
evidence.quote: The research reported here assessed the math anxiety of 17 first- and second-grade female teachers from a large midwestern urban school district. The math achievement of the students in these teachers' classrooms, along with students' beliefs about gender and academic success in domains like math, was also assessed.
A total of 117 students (65 girls and 52 boys) participated.

Math anxiety was assessed using the 25-item short Mathematics Anxiety Rating Scale. Math achievement was measured using the Applied Problems subtest of the Woodcock-Johnson III Tests of Achievement. Students' gender ability beliefs were assessed by drawings after two gender-neutral stories.

By the end of the school year, the higher a teacher's math anxiety, the lower was the girls' but not the boys' math achievement. The relation between teacher anxiety and girls' achievement became nonsignificant when girls' gender ability beliefs were also used to predict achievement.

original.claim: Adults tend by default to treat immoral and irrational events as impossible.
original.method: Three sets of studies compared adults' quick default judgments with reflective possibility judgments, then tested modal verbs and judgments of whether an agent was forced to act.
original.population: Amazon Mechanical Turk adults across nine samples; individual samples ranged from 61 to 498 participants.
original.outcome_measure: Judgments of whether events were possible under default versus deliberative reasoning.

evidence.quote: We present three studies that characterize the role of implicit representations of possibility in cognition. Collectively, these studies differentiate explicit reasoning about possibilities from default implicit representations, demonstrate that human adults often default to treating immoral and irrational events as impossible.

All participants were recruited from Amazon Mechanical Turk. Sample sizes and demographic information are as follows: study 1a (judgments of possibility), 498 participants; study 1b (event ratings), 61 participants.

original.claim: Deactivating Facebook for one week lowers users' regard for ethnic outgroups in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
original.method: Eligible Facebook users were block-randomized to deactivate their profile or remain active during the week around July 2019 genocide remembrance, then completed an endline survey.
original.population: Facebook users in Bosnia and Herzegovina; 353 completed the endline survey (159 deactivation, 194 control).
original.outcome_measure: A composite index of attitudes toward ethnic outgroups, measured in the endline survey.

evidence.quote: We report results from a randomized controlled trial in Bosnia and Herzegovina (BiH), exploring the effects of exposure to social media during 1 wk around genocide remembrance in July 2019 on a set of interethnic attitudes of Facebook users. We find evidence that ... people who deactivated their Facebook profiles report lower regard for ethnic outgroups than those who remained active.
We block randomized the 556 resulting individuals into treatment and control ... We received endline surveys from 159 participants in the treatment group and 194 participants in the control group.

original.claim: Making God salient reduced preference for human over algorithmic recommendations across decision contexts.
original.method: US participants were randomly assigned to write about God or their day, then compared human and algorithm recommendations across 24 tasks.
original.population: The Study 1 analytic sample comprised 321 US-based Prolific participants with a mean age of 37.8 years.
original.outcome_measure: A 101-point relative-preference scale for algorithm versus equally effective human recommendations, averaged across 24 tasks.

evidence.quote: After the writing task, participants were given a list of 24 tasks, and they indicated on a 101-point scale their relative likelihood of following the recommendation of a computer algorithm over that of an equally effective human counterpart for each task.

We recruited 405 US-based participants on Prolific. The final sample of 321 participants was randomly assigned to one of the two conditions. In the high salience condition, participants were asked to write about the role or impact of God in their lives. In the low salience condition, they wrote about the things they have done during the day.
Participants’ preference for receiving recommendations from humans was significantly lower when they were reminded of God.

original.claim: The number of Facebook friends was positively associated with grey-matter density in focal temporal and entorhinal regions.
original.method: Healthy adults underwent MRI scanning and researchers recorded each participant's Facebook friend count for voxel-based morphometry analyses.
original.population: One hundred twenty-five healthy University College London community participants took part in the MRI experiment.
original.outcome_measure: Facebook friend count and regional grey-matter density measured by voxel-based morphometry.

evidence.quote: Quantitative variation in the number of friends an individual declares on a web-based social networking service reliably predicted grey matter density in the right superior temporal sulcus, left middle temporal gyrus and entorhinal cortex.

One hundred and twenty-five healthy participants recruited from the local community of University College London took part in experiment 1. After MRI scanning, the number of friends for that individual in their Facebook public profile was recorded.

original.claim: Young adults assigned to cognitive-reminiscence therapy scored higher than waitlist controls on self-esteem, self-efficacy, meaning in life, and optimism after the three sessions.
original.method: A two-arm randomized trial assigned participants to three sessions of cognitive-reminiscence therapy or a waitlist control.
original.population: Sixty-two young adults residing in Australia aged 18–29 completed the study (31 therapy; 31 control).
original.outcome_measure: Self-esteem, self-efficacy, meaning in life, and optimism scales were the primary outcomes.

evidence.quote: The primary outcomes were psychological resources of self-esteem, self-efficacy, meaning in life, and optimism.
The study used a randomised controlled trial design with two arms (CRT; waitlist control) and three time-points (baseline; post-third session of CRT; 2-week follow-up).
A total of 62 participants (31 CRT; 31 control) completed the study and were included in the final analysis.

A community sample of young adults was recruited between June and September 2020 using advertisements distributed via social media and snowball sampling. Inclusion criteria were: aged between 18 to 29 years (representing emerging adulthood, Arnett et al., 2014), fluency in English, residing in Australia and internet access in the home.

The results of the ANCOVA analyses, which adjusted for baseline scores, showed the CRT group was significantly higher in all four measures of psychological resources than the control group after the last session of CRT and at the 2-week follow-up.

original.claim: Higher COVID-19-related anxiety was associated with more general, gastrointestinal, and fatigue somatic symptoms after covariate adjustment.
original.method: A stratified-quota online survey of UK adults estimated regression associations between COVID-19 anxiety quintiles and somatic-symptom scores with demographic, health, and generalized-anxiety covariates.
original.population: The sample comprised 2,025 UK adults recruited from an online research panel to match the UK population on sex, age, income, and region.
original.outcome_measure: COVID-19 anxiety and Patient Health Questionnaire-15 total and subscale somatic-symptom scores.

evidence.quote: This study aimed to estimate the association between anxiety associated with COVID-19 and somatic symptoms, using data from a large, representative sample (N = 2,025) of the UK adult population. Moderate to high levels of anxiety associated with COVID-19 were significantly associated with general somatic symptoms and in particular with gastrointestinal and fatigue symptoms.

Participants were recruited from an online research panel using stratified quota sampling to ensure that sex, age, household income, and region matched the UK population. Regression models estimated the relationship between COVID-19 anxiety quintiles and the PHQ-15 subscales, with age, gender, income, pre-existing health problems, and generalized anxiety included as covariates.

Somatic symptoms were measured using the Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-15), a 15-item self-report measure. The total scale scores and subscales reflecting pain, gastrointestinal, cardiopulmonary, and fatigue symptoms were used.

original.claim: After seeing one English-speaking and one Spanish-speaking actor, 9-month-old infants looked longer at their affiliative than disengagement interactions.
original.method: Infants watched actors who spoke either the same or different languages and then viewed alternating affiliative and disengagement interactions.
original.population: Thirty-two 9-month-old infants from monolingual English-speaking homes participated.
original.outcome_measure: Looking time to the screen after each affiliative or disengagement test video was measured.

evidence.quote: Infants in the English-Spanish condition looked significantly longer at affiliation events (M =17.0 seconds, SD =8.2 seconds) than disengagement events (M =10.0 seconds, SD =4.2 seconds).
Thirty-two 9-month-old infants (18 female; M age = 9 months, 3 days; range= 8;15– 9;17) participated. All infants were from monolingual English-speaking homes according to parental report.
For test trials, we used repeated-measures ANOVAs with attention to the screen (in seconds) after the test movies had ended as the dependent variable.

Infants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Infants in the English-Spanish condition watched videos where one actor spoke English and the other actor spoke Spanish. Following familiarization, all infants viewed six alternating test trials in which the actors interacted positively by affiliating or interacted negatively by socially disengaging.

original.claim: Fourteen-month-old infants who bounced in synchrony with an adult showed more spontaneous helping than infants who bounced asynchronously.
original.method: Infants were bounced to music while an experimenter bounced either in synchrony or asynchronously, then completed object-return helping tasks.
original.population: Forty-eight walking infants from English-speaking homes completed Experiment 1 (mean age 14.2 months).
original.outcome_measure: Video-coded spontaneous helping within the first 10 seconds of object-return trials was measured.

evidence.quote: Raters also recorded elapsed time before helping occurred, to calculate scores for spontaneous helping (0-10 s into trial, while experimenter focuses only on the object).

Thus there were four bounce conditions: synchronous bouncing/evenly spaced beats; synchronous bouncing/unevenly spaced beats; asynchronous bouncing/evenly spaced beats; asynchronous bouncing/unevenly spaced beats.
The assistant and experimenter bounced for 145 s according to the bounce instructions while the infant listened to the melodic stimuli.
Forty-eight walking infants from English-speaking homes (24 girls; M age=14.2 months; SD=0.2 months) completed the experiment.

evidence.location: Experiment 1, Results, Spontaneous and delayed helping (p. 10)
evidence.quote: Infants were significantly more likely to demonstrate spontaneous helping following interpersonal synchrony (25.8%, SEM=4.3%) compared to interpersonal asynchrony (13.1%, SEM=3.9%).

original.claim: Participants receiving left-DLPFC high-definition transcranial direct-current stimulation reported lower mind-wandering scores during stimulation than sham participants.
original.method: In a double-blind sham-controlled study, participants completed a finger-tapping random-sequence task during active or sham left-DLPFC stimulation.
original.population: Study 3 recruited 60 adults aged 18–50 through university-campus flyers, social media, and personal contacts.
original.outcome_measure: Periodic thought probes rated task focus from completely focused to completely unfocused.

evidence.quote: When applying a high-definition transcranial direct-current stimulation (HD-tDCS) montage to the left DLPFC, we find that propensity to mind wander is reduced relative to a group receiving sham stimulation.

evidence.location: General methods: Finger-tapping random-sequence generation task
evidence.quote: Concretely, participants were instructed to press two buttons with their left or right index finger in a random order.
Subjects stimulated with real HD-tDCS reported lower mind wandering scores during stimulation than the group receiving sham stimulation.

Approximately every minute (minimally 40 s, maximally 80 s, uniformly distributed), a thought-probe was presented asking how focused the participant was on the task (1 = ‘completely focused’, 4 = ‘completely unfocused’, 10 and 20 thought-probes in the baseline online sessions respectively).
We implemented a double-blind, sham-controlled design and randomly assigned half of our subjects to a sham and the other half to the real stimulation group.
A total of 60 participants (19 male) were recruited with flyers on the university campus, on social media networks and by personal contacts.

Inclusion criteria were a signed informed consent-form, aged between 18- and 50-years, no psychiatric/neurological condition (e.g. depression, bipolar disorder, epilepsy, migraine, severe head trauma, brain surgery) currently or in the past, not under the influence of psychotropic drugs (except caffeine and nicotine), not taking central nervous system medications (e.g. antidepressants, antiepileptic drugs), good or corrected eyesight and that they reported to have slept enough during the preceding night.

original.claim: Six-month-old infants preferred numerically changing image streams at 1:2, 1:3, and 1:4 ratios, but not at a 2:3 ratio.
original.method: Infants viewed simultaneous changing and non-changing dot-image streams across five numerical-ratio conditions.
original.population: Eighty 6-month-old infants participated in Experiment 1.
original.outcome_measure: The preference score was the difference between looking time to changing and non-changing streams.

evidence.location: Materials and methods, Experiment 1, Data analysis
evidence.quote: We then calculated preference scores for each infant by subtracting the average percent looking time to the non-changing image stream from the percent looking time to the changing image stream across the four trials.

Infants were presented with two image streams simultaneously on two peripheral screens. In one of the image streams, images alternated between two different numbers of dots, while the other image stream only contained images with the same number of dots.
Infants were randomly assigned to one of five conditions: 6vs24 (1:4 ratio), 6vs18 (1:3 ratio), 10vs20 (1:2 ratio), 8vs16 (1:2 ratio), and 12vs18 (2:3 ratio).
Eighty infants with a mean age of 6 months and 1 day participated, 16 in each of five conditions.

evidence.location: Results, Ratio-modulation of number discrimination at 6 months (Experiment 1)
evidence.quote: There was a significant preference for the changing stream for the 1:4, 1:3, and 1:2 ratio conditions, but not for the 2:3 ratio condition.

original.claim: During feature search, frontal-eye-field movement activity began earlier in efficient than inefficient search, and that onset difference matched the reaction-time difference.
original.method: Macaques performed efficient and inefficient visual-search tasks while frontal-eye-field movement-related neurons were recorded.
original.population: Four macaque monkeys contributed to the color and motion feature-search tasks.
original.outcome_measure: Reaction time and the onset time of frontal-eye-field movement-related neural activity were measured.

evidence.quote: Four macaque monkeys (Macaca radiata and M. mulatta) participated in the color and motion search tasks.
Fifty-eight movement-related neurons recorded from 5 monkeys had sufficient data for these analyses (40 neurons recorded during feature search and 18 neurons during spatial-configuration search).
Using juice-reinforced operant conditioning, monkeys were trained to produce one saccade to foveate a target in a visual search array.

evidence.location: Results, Color and motion feature search
evidence.quote: Mean RT across all motion and color feature-search trials was significantly faster in the efficient search condition (195.4 ms) compared to the inefficient condition (245.5 ms).

evidence.location: Results, Color and motion feature search
evidence.quote: The average beginning of movement-related activation across the 40 neurons was significantly earlier during efficient (83.7 ms) compared to inefficient (133.8 ms) search. Notably, the difference between beginning times of movement-related activity between search conditions (50.1 ms) corresponded quantitatively to the RT difference between search conditions (50.05 ms).

original.claim: Higher well-being was associated with less small talk and more substantive conversation.
original.method: Undergraduates wore the Electronically Activated Recorder for four days; coders classified sampled recordings, and well-being was assessed with self- and informant-report measures.
original.population: Seventy-nine undergraduates, including 47 women, provided four days of naturalistic recordings.
original.outcome_measure: Relative frequencies of small-talk and substantive conversations, related to a composite well-being index, life satisfaction, and happiness ratings.

evidence.quote: Seventy-nine undergraduates (47 females) wore the EAR for four days. The EAR recorded for 30 seconds every 12.5 minutes, providing 23,689 waking recordings. For each recording, coders identified whether a participant was alone, talking with others, and whether a conversation was small talk or substantive.
To obtain a multi-method well-being index, we combined the self- and informant-based happiness measure with participants’ self-reported life satisfaction.
Higher well-being was associated with having less small talk, r = -.33, and more substantive conversations, r = .28.

original.claim: Science interest was a stronger predictor of science achievement in higher socioeconomic contexts and higher-GDP countries.
original.method: Researchers analyzed the PISA 2006 international assessment using multilevel interaction models of student science interest, socioeconomic context, and science achievement.
original.population: The dataset included 398,750 representative 15-year-old students from 57 nations.
original.outcome_measure: PISA science-literacy plausible values and a composite self-reported science-interest score.

evidence.quote: In a dataset drawn from approximately 400,000 high school students from 57 countries, student interest in science is a substantially stronger predictor of science achievement in higher socioeconomic contexts and in higher GDP nations.

The 2006 dataset contains 398,750 individual student participants selected to be representative of the general population of 15 year old students from 57 nations. PISA measured participants using a test assessing multiple areas of science achievement.

evidence.location: Method: Science Interest and Science Self-Concept
evidence.quote: To index science interest, we selected five survey items about having fun learning science, liking reading about science, enjoying science problems, enjoying acquiring new science knowledge, and being interested in learning science.

original.claim: The generalized-anxiety groups showed faster disengagement from angry and fearful faces than comparison groups.
original.method: Clinically screened generalized-anxiety patients, matched volunteers, and high-trait-anxiety participants completed a computerized face-cue attentional task.
original.population: Experiment 1 included 14 generalized-anxiety patients, 14 matched healthy relatives, and 14 high-trait-anxiety participants without generalized-anxiety disorder.
original.outcome_measure: Reaction times to identify a target letter appearing around angry, happy, or neutral face cues.
