evidence.quote: Across two experiments we found faster disengagement from negative (angry and fearful) faces in generalized anxiety disorder groups.

A total of 14 generalized anxiety disorder patients, 14 of their relatives (matched healthy volunteers), and 14 people with high levels of self-reported trait anxiety who did not pass criteria for generalized anxiety disorder took part in the study.

Participants saw a face followed by a letter either X or P above, below, to the left, or to the right of the face. They were instructed to categorize the letter as quickly and accurately as possible by pressing a response button. Reaction times were recorded with 1-ms accuracy.

original.claim: Children with recent suicidal ideation showed a smaller reward-positivity difference between monetary gains and losses than matched children without recent ideation.
original.method: Children completed a 50-trial monetary guessing task while continuous electroencephalography isolated the Reward Positivity event-related potential.
original.population: Twenty-three community-recruited children aged 7 to 11 years with recent suicidal ideation were matched to 46 children without recent ideation.
original.outcome_measure: The Reward Positivity difference between neural responses to monetary gains and losses.

evidence.quote: Children with recent SI exhibited significantly smaller (i.e., blunted) ΔRewP.

Participants were 23 children between the ages of 7 and 11 with a history of recent suicidal ideation and 46 demographically and clinically matched children with no recent suicidal ideation. Children completed a simple guessing task during which continuous electroencephalography was recorded to isolate the Reward Positivity event-related potential, which reflects the difference in neural responses to monetary gains versus losses.

original.claim: Taxometric analyses favored a dimensional rather than categorical latent structure for cannabis dependence.
original.method: Researchers applied MAXEIG and MAMBAC taxometric analyses, with simulated comparison data, to DSM-IV cannabis-dependence indicators.
original.population: The analytic sample comprised 1,474 cannabis-using respondents to the 2001–2002 National Epidemiologic Survey on Alcohol and Related Conditions.
original.outcome_measure: Seven dichotomous DSM-IV cannabis-dependence criteria used as indicators in the taxometric analyses.

evidence.quote: MAXEIG and MAMBAC were conducted on data from 1,474 cannabis-using respondents to the 2001–2002 National Epidemiologic Survey on Alcohol and Related Conditions. Respondents answered questions assessing DSM-IV criteria for cannabis dependence.

Both taxometric methods provided support for a dimensional structure of cannabis dependence. Although the MAMBAC results were not entirely unequivocal, the majority of evidence favored a dimensional structure of cannabis dependence.

Our analytic strategy consisted of two taxometric methods: MAXEIG and MAMBAC. For each method, we created 10 dimensional and 10 taxonic simulated data sets based on the distributional features of the research data.

original.claim: Participants in a short pre-college STEM Academy reported increased science identity and belonging to STEM and the university.
original.method: First-time college STEM students completed psychosocial surveys before and after a short cocurricular STEM Academy and were compared with matched non-Academy students.
original.population: The Academy group contained 109 first-time college STEM students at the University of South Florida; 99 completed both pre- and post-program surveys.
original.outcome_measure: Likert-scale self-report measures of science identity and belonging to STEM and the university.

evidence.quote: A cohort of diverse freshman entering a large urban research university showed increased science identity and sense of belonging to STEM and to the university after a short cocurricular STEM Academy.

First-time in college STEM students participated in the Academy program, with a non-Academy first-year STEM group used for comparison. All psychosocial measures included self-report scales rated on a Likert rating system.
All participants were students at the University of South Florida. The final N of the STEM Academy was 109. Ninety-nine students were included in the pre–post survey analysis.

original.claim: Three months of intensive meditation training produced a smaller attentional blink and a smaller T1-elicited P3b.
original.method: Meditation practitioners and novice controls completed an attentional-blink task while scalp EEG was recorded before and after training periods.
original.population: 17 participants at a three-month meditation retreat and 23 novice participants interested in meditation.
original.outcome_measure: Attentional-blink task accuracy and the T1-elicited P3b brain-potential measure.

evidence.quote: Three months of intensive mental training resulted in a smaller attentional blink and reduced brain-resource allocation to the first target, as reflected by a smaller T1-elicited P3b, a brain-potential index of resource allocation.
Participants performed four blocks of 102 trials of the attentional-blink task while their EEG was recorded. EEG was recorded at 512 Hz from 64 Ag–AgCl electrodes.

Data were collected from 17 participants at the beginning and end of a 3-mo meditation retreat during which they meditated for 10–12 h per day (practitioner group). Control data were collected from 23 participants interested in learning about meditation (novice group). ... In each session, participants performed an attentional-blink task in which they had to identify two targets (both numbers) embedded in a rapid stream of distracter letters.

original.claim: In two magpies, mark-directed behavior was significantly enhanced only when a colored mark was visible in a mirror.
original.method: Hand-raised magpies underwent open-mirror exploration, mirror-preference testing, and mark tests with reflective and nonreflective control conditions.
original.population: Five adult hand-raised magpies.
original.outcome_measure: Mirror-directed, social, contingent, and mark-directed self-behaviors.

evidence.quote: Five adult hand-raised magpies served as subjects throughout the study. ... Investigation of behavior towards a mirror consisted of three steps. Open mirror exploration. ... Mirror preference and standardized mirror exploration. ... Mark test. In the mark test, each subject was involved in eight test sessions with the conditions, (1) mirror and colored mark, (2) mirror and black mark, (3) no mirror and colored mark, and (4) no mirror and black mark.

evidence.location: Materials and Methods — Scoring of behaviors (PDF pp. 7–8)
evidence.quote: We recorded all behaviors directed towards a bird’s own body ... and we assessed whether the action was directed towards the regions near the mark or elsewhere. ... From videotapes, the frequency of behaviors directed towards the own body were scored.

In the subsequent quantitative analysis, which compared the behavior in the mirror and mark condition with a condition without a mirror, mark-directed behavior in two of the birds, Gerti and Goldie, was significantly higher in the critical mirror and mark condition than in the other conditions. ... Mark-directed behavior was only significantly enhanced when a mirror was present and the mark was colored and thus visible for the birds.

original.claim: Chromosome 9p21.3 loci were associated with risk of aggressive periodontitis as well as coronary heart disease.
original.method: Researchers conducted candidate-gene association analyses in coronary-heart-disease and aggressive-periodontitis samples.
original.population: German coronary-heart-disease samples including 1,104 early-onset patients and 736 healthy controls, plus 159 aggressive-periodontitis patients.
original.outcome_measure: Association of chromosome 9p21.3 variants with coronary heart disease and aggressive periodontitis risk.

evidence.quote: In a candidate-gene association study, we identify an association of a genetic susceptibility locus shared by both diseases. We confirm the known association of two neighboring linkage disequilibrium regions on human chromosome 9p21.3 with CHD and show the additional strong association of these loci with the risk of aggressive periodontitis.
SNPs in 159 German periodontitis patients with the most extreme phenotype of generalized aggressive periodontitis
large population of 1,104 early-onset CHD patients... and 736 healthy ethnically matched controls

original.claim: Variants in and around PTPRD and SRR were associated with type 2 diabetes susceptibility in the Han Chinese study samples.
original.method: A two-stage genome-wide association study genotyped an initial case-control sample and a second-stage sample.
original.population: 995 type-2-diabetes patients and 894 controls in stage 1, with 1,803 patients and 1,473 controls in stage 2.
original.outcome_measure: Genetic association with type 2 diabetes case-control status.

evidence.quote: A two-stage genome-wide association (GWA) study was conducted, in which 995 patients and 894 controls were genotyped ... 1,803 patients and 1,473 controls in stage 2.
We found two loci not previously associated with diabetes susceptibility in and around the genes protein tyrosine phosphatase receptor type D (PTPRD) and serine racemase (SRR).

original.claim: Greater genome-wide autozygosity was associated with higher odds of schizophrenia.
original.method: Researchers used runs of homozygosity in imputed genome-wide SNP data to estimate autozygous tracts and test case-control association.
original.population: 9,388 schizophrenia cases and 12,456 controls across 17 case-control datasets.
original.outcome_measure: Schizophrenia case-control status and the proportion of autosomes in autozygous tracts.

evidence.quote: Here, we use runs of homozygosity in genome-wide SNP data to estimate the proportion of the autosome that exists in autozygous tracts in 9,388 cases with schizophrenia and 12,456 controls.
We estimate that the odds of schizophrenia increase by ~17% for every 1% increase in genome-wide autozygosity.

original.claim: Over 24 months, five repeat suicide attempts occurred in the ASSIP group versus 41 in the usual-treatment group.
original.method: Recently suicidal patients were randomly assigned to usual treatment or usual treatment plus three ASSIP sessions and personalized follow-up letters over 24 months.
original.population: 120 patients who had recently attempted suicide, 60 assigned to each treatment condition.
original.outcome_measure: Repeat suicide attempts, suicidal ideation, depression, and health-care utilization over 24 months.

evidence.quote: Patients who had recently attempted suicide were randomly allocated to treatment as usual (n = 60) or treatment as usual plus ASSIP (n = 60). ASSIP participants received three therapy sessions followed by regular contact through personalized letters over 24 months. ... During the 24-month follow-up period, five repeat suicide attempts were recorded in the ASSIP group and 41 attempts in the control group.

Study participants completed a set of psychosocial and clinical questionnaires every 6 months over a 24-month follow-up period. The primary outcome measure was repeat suicide attempts during the 24-month follow-up period. Secondary outcome measures were suicidal ideation, depression, and health-care utilization.

original.claim: Participants' retrospective estimates made their own frightening free fall seem longer, without evidence of increased temporal resolution during the fall.
original.method: Researchers measured participants' digit-discrimination threshold with a wrist-mounted device before and during a free fall into a safety net.
original.population: 20 participants tested during daytime or nighttime free-fall sessions.
original.outcome_measure: Digit-discrimination temporal threshold and retrospective estimates of fall duration.

evidence.quote: Using a hand-held device to measure speed of visual perception, participants experienced free fall for 31 m before landing safely in a net. We found no evidence of increased temporal resolution, in apparent conflict with the fact that participants retrospectively estimated their own fall to last 36% longer than others' falls.
We tested 13 participants during the daytime and 7 at nighttime

original.claim: A twelve-hour interval containing sleep improves verbal recall and resistance to later interference compared with a wake interval.
original.method: Participants learned word pairs, spent twelve hours in a sleep or wake condition, learned interfering pairs, and completed cued recall of the original and interfering responses.
original.population: 45 right-handed, native-English-speaking participants aged 18 to 22, randomly assigned to Sleep or Wake.
original.outcome_measure: Cued recall of learned A-B word pairs after a twelve-hour delay and after A-C interference learning.

evidence.quote: We compared memory recall after sleep, with and without interference before testing. We demonstrated that recall performance for verbal memory was greater after sleep than after wakefulness. And when using interference testing, that difference was even more pronounced.

Forty-five participants (ages 18–22) were enrolled and successfully completed the study. Forty-five participants were randomly assigned to one of two groups: Sleep or Wake. Each participant initially learned 60 paired associates (A–B).

original.claim: Playing Tetris after a traumatic film significantly reduced flashback frequency over one week compared with no task.
original.method: Participants watched a traumatic film, completed a structured break, and were randomly assigned to 10 minutes of Tetris or no task before one week of monitoring.
original.population: 40 participants, 20 assigned to each condition.
original.outcome_measure: One-week flashback frequency, PTSD symptomatology, and recognition memory.

evidence.location: Abstract — Methodology and Principal Findings (PDF p. 1)
evidence.quote: Flashbacks were monitored for 1-week. Results indicated that compared to the no-task condition, the ‘Tetris’ condition produced a significant reduction in flashback frequency over 1-week. Convergent results were found on a clinical measure of PTSD symptomatology at 1-week. Recognition memory between groups did not differ significantly.

We were interested in testing whether a cognitive intervention—a visuospatial task—could modulate later flashbacks to traumatic material. ... Forty participants watched a 12-min film of traumatic scenes of injury and death (n = 20 per group). Film viewing was followed by a 30-min interval. Participants were then randomly allocated to the visuospatial task condition, playing ‘Tetris’ for 10-min, or the no-task control condition.

original.claim: Post-earthquake concern about safety and health decreased as residential devastation level increased.
original.method: Researchers surveyed adults in devastated and non-devastated Chinese areas with a five-question safety-and-health questionnaire.
original.population: 2,262 adults: 1,720 from devastated areas and 542 from non-devastated areas.
original.outcome_measure: Questionnaire estimates concerning safety measures, epidemic disease, medical workers, psychological workers, and medication.

evidence.quote: The post-earthquake concern decreased significantly as the level of residential devastation increased.

we surveyed a convenience sample of 2,262 adults on their post-earthquake concern about safety and health. Residents in non-devastated areas... and devastated areas... responded to a questionnaire of 5 questions regarding safety measures, epidemic disease, medical workers, psychological workers, and medication.

original.claim: A metaphorical framing of crime changes the solutions and further information people choose.
original.method: In five online experiments, participants read crime reports framed with a metaphor such as a virus or a beast, then recommended solutions or selected information for decisions.
original.population: Online U.S. participants recruited through Amazon Mechanical Turk; analyzed experiment samples included 253, 236, and 178 participants.
original.outcome_measure: Recommended crime-control solutions, chosen information, and reports of what influenced participants' decisions.

evidence.quote: In five experiments, we explore how these metaphors influence the way that we reason about complex issues and forage for further information about them. We find that even the subtlest instantiation of a metaphor (via a single word) can have a powerful influence over how people attempt to solve social problems like crime and how they gather information to make 'well-informed' decisions.

All five experiments were conducted online with participants recruited from Amazon's Mechanical Turk ... We used Mechanical Turk's exclusion capabilities and tracked IP addresses to ensure that participants were not repeatedly sampled.
This left data from 253 participants for analysis ... This left data from 236 participants for analysis ... This left data from 178 participants for analysis.

original.claim: Reluctance to share research data was associated with weaker statistical evidence and more apparent reporting errors.
original.method: Researchers related authors' data-sharing decisions to reported statistical results and apparent reporting errors in published papers.
original.population: 49 psychology papers containing 1,148 statistically significant results.
original.outcome_measure: Data-sharing willingness, strength of reported evidence, and apparent errors in statistical reporting.

evidence.quote: We found the reluctance to share data to be associated with weaker evidence... and a higher prevalence of apparent errors in the reporting of statistical results.
We related the reluctance to share research data for reanalysis to 1148 statistically significant results reported in 49 papers published in two major psychology journals.

original.claim: The study estimated a large multivariate sex difference across measured personality dimensions.
original.method: Researchers used multigroup latent-variable modeling of 16PF questionnaire data and combined dimension-level differences into a Mahalanobis D value.
original.population: 10,261 adults in a demographically representative U.S. standardization sample.
original.outcome_measure: Latent 16PF personality dimensions and their aggregated Mahalanobis D difference.

evidence.quote: Personality measures were obtained from a large US sample (N = 10,261) with the 16PF Questionnaire. Multigroup latent variable modeling was used to estimate sex differences on individual personality dimensions, which were then aggregated to yield a multivariate effect size (Mahalanobis D).
We found a global effect size D = 2.71, corresponding to an overlap of only 10% between the male and female distributions.

original.claim: Participants favored more masculine-looking leaders in conflict scenarios and more feminine-looking leaders in cooperative scenarios.
original.method: Across rating and mock-election tasks, researchers varied face masculinity or femininity and intergroup conflict or cooperation context.
original.population: 38 UK students, 46 Indonesian students, and 118 online volunteers across three experiments.
original.outcome_measure: Ratings and choices of facial suitability for leadership in conflict and cooperation scenarios.

evidence.quote: Across two experiments we show that a general categorization of leader versus nonleader is an initial implicit requirement for emergence, and at a context-specific level facial cues of masculinity and femininity contingently affect war versus peace leadership emergence in the predicted direction.
Thirty-eight participants... volunteered
The sample consisted solely of Indonesian students... and included 46 participants... One hundred and eighteen participants... were recruited... to complete this online study.

We manipulated the intention to resolve this conflict through dominant (war) or peaceful means... participants... voted for one of the two faces they felt would be most suited as leader in that scenario.

original.claim: Toddlers showed greater happiness when giving treats to others than when receiving treats, especially when giving their own treat.
original.method: Researchers coded toddlers' happiness while children received treats, gave an experimenter-provided treat to a puppet, and gave their own treat to a puppet.
original.population: 20 healthy full-term toddlers in the main study, aged about 22 to 23 months.
original.outcome_measure: Coded happiness during receiving, non-costly giving, and costly giving phases.

evidence.quote: the present study finds that before the age of two, toddlers exhibit greater happiness when giving treats to others than receiving treats themselves. Further, children are happier after engaging in costly giving... than when giving the same treat at no cost.
Twenty toddlers (11 boys, Xage = 22 months, 26 days, range 22;7 to 23;17) participated.
Participants’ happiness during each phase was coded... Next, the experimenter... asked the child to give it to the puppet, and... asked the child to give the puppet a treat from the child’s own bowl

original.claim: The rs978739 polymorphism upstream of TAS2R16 was associated with longevity in the study population.
original.method: Researchers genotyped common variation in bitter-taste receptor gene clusters and tested its association with longevity.
original.population: 941 unrelated people from Calabria, Italy: 348 very elderly cases and 593 non-elderly controls.
original.outcome_measure: Genotype association with case-control longevity status.

evidence.quote: We found that one polymorphism, rs978739, situated 212 bp upstream of the TAS2R16 gene, shows a statistically significant association... with longevity.
We investigated the association between the common genetic variation at the three bitter taste gene clusters on chromosomes 5, 7 and 12 and longevity
Subjects were recruited between 1994 and 2008 in Calabria and included 941 unrelated individuals, of which 348 were very elderly cases... and 593 were non-elderly controls

original.claim: A TCF4 TGC repeat length above 50 was more frequent in severe Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy cases than in normal-cornea controls.
original.method: A three-stage genetic association study determined TCF4 repeat length with PCR, sequencing, STR assay, and Southern blotting.
original.population: 66 participants with severe Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy and 63 participants with normal corneas.
original.outcome_measure: TCF4 intronic TGC repeat length.

evidence.quote: Compiling data for 3 arms of the study, a TGC repeat length >50 was present in 79% of FECD cases and in 3% of normal controls cases

We tested for an association between an intronic TGC trinucleotide repeat in TCF4 and FECD by determining repeat length in 66 affected participants with severe FECD and 63 participants with normal corneas. PCR primers flanking the TGC repeat were used to amplify leukocyte-derived genomic DNA. Repeat length was determined by direct sequencing, short tandem repeat (STR) assay and Southern blotting.

original.claim: Baseline plasma oxytocin showed a U-shaped association with trust in the trust game.
original.method: Researchers measured baseline plasma oxytocin and observed trust and trustworthiness in a one-shot trust game.
original.population: 1,158 undergraduate Han Chinese students at the National University of Singapore.
original.outcome_measure: Baseline plasma oxytocin, trust, and trustworthiness in a one-shot trust game.

evidence.quote: Using a large sample of 1,158 participants, we observed a significant U-shaped relationship between plasma OT with the level of trust, and marginally with the level of trustworthiness
we measured base-line plasma OT levels in a very large sample of 1,158 undergraduate Han Chinese students at the National University of Singapore who participated in one-shot TG.

original.claim: Participants favoring conservative presidents were less likely than those favoring liberal presidents to agree to write a counter-attitudinal political essay under high choice.
original.method: Two online experiments asked U.S. participants to write political and non-political counter-attitudinal essays under high- or low-choice instructions.
original.population: 180 U.S. online participants in the first experiment and 159 in the second.
original.outcome_measure: Whether participants complied with the request to write a counter-attitudinal essay.

evidence.quote: U.S. residents who preferred more conservative presidents... complied less than Americans who preferred more liberal presidents... with the request to write a counter-attitudinal essay about who made a ‘better president.’

we asked participants to write two counter-attitudinal essays, one on the subject of presidents and another on the subject of computers... Participants assigned to the high choice condition were able to respond ‘yes’ or ‘no’ to the request

One hundred and eighty participants... in the United States were recruited online through Amazon's Mechanical Turk... One hundred fifty-nine participants... in the U.S. were recruited online through Amazon's Mechanical Turk

original.claim: When the reference was a main meal alone, participants estimated fewer calories for a test meal with a healthy side than for the test meal alone; the pattern reversed when the reference also had a healthy side.
original.method: In Study 3, adults first saw a 500-calorie reference meal with or without a healthy side, then estimated calories and healthiness for a cheeseburger shown with or without celery.
original.population: Study 3 included 430 U.S. adults over age 18 recruited through an online panel.
original.outcome_measure: Calorie estimates and healthiness ratings of meals and food combinations.

evidence.quote: Analyses of variance were planned on calorie estimates including a main effect of the healthy side in the test food, a main effect of the healthy side in the reference food, and an interaction between the presence of a side in the test food with the presence of a side in the reference food.
430 participants, all residents of the United States of America and over 18 years, were recruited via an online panel.

After consenting to take part in the study, participants were randomly allocated to one of four groups in a 2 by 2 design. Participants were shown a reference meal, which was always labeled as containing 500 calories, followed by a test meal and asked to estimate the calorie content of the test meal. The reference food used in this study was a simple hamburger (with carrot batons), and the test food used in this study was a cheeseburger (with celery sticks).

When the reference food was a main meal alone, the test food with a healthy side was estimated to have fewer calories than the test food alone. By contrast, when the reference food included a healthy side, the test food with a healthy side was estimated to have more calories that the test food alone.

original.claim: People who show greater self-control avoid a task that demands cognitive control, indicating an intrinsic cost of self-control.
original.method: Students completed an intertemporal-choice task, a free-choice demand-selection task, and a self-control questionnaire in counterbalanced order.
original.population: 50 Princeton University students, ages 18 to 24.
original.outcome_measure: Demand avoidance in the demand-selection task, intertemporal choices, and self-control-scale scores.

evidence.quote: We show that people who show more self-control in intertemporal choice also avoid task demands, providing support for the idea that self-control is intrinsically costly.

evidence.location: Materials and Methods > Participants and Procedure
evidence.quote: Fifty students from the Princeton University (31 females, 18–24 years) participated ... All participants performed an ITC task and the DST, with order counterbalanced across participants, followed by completion of the Self-Control Scale.

original.claim: Musical sophistication in non-musicians can be measured across distinct dimensions using a new self-report inventory.
original.method: A large internet survey was used to develop and test a musical-sophistication inventory, followed by laboratory measures of perceptual ability.
original.population: 147,636 general-population internet participants; development and test samples contained 73,894 and 73,739 respondents.
original.outcome_measure: Self-reported musical behaviors and skills, plus laboratory measures of perceptual musical ability.

evidence.quote: We present a new self-report inventory, the Goldsmiths Musical Sophistication Index (Gold-MSI), which allows us to measure five dimensions in the general population using a large Internet sample (n = 147,636).
Study 1 reports the development of the inventory from a large sample gathered through an online survey ... the full sample into a training dataset (n = 73,894) ... and a test dataset (n = 73,739).

original.claim: Two minutes of whole-body vibration improved attention in healthy participants and adults diagnosed with ADHD.
original.method: In a repeated-measures design, participants received passive whole-body vibration while seated and completed a color-word interference task.
original.population: 83 healthy university students and 17 university students diagnosed with ADHD.
original.outcome_measure: Attention measured as inhibitory control on a color-word interference paradigm.

evidence.quote: Eighty-three healthy individuals and seventeen adults diagnosed with ADHD participated in the study. WBV treatment was applied passively, while participants were sitting on a chair which was mounted on a vibrating platform. A repeated measure design was employed... Attention (i.e. inhibitory control) was measured with a color-word interference paradigm.
A period of two minutes of WBV treatment had significant beneficial effects of small to medium size on attention of both healthy individuals and adults with ADHD.

original.claim: Words studied in metaphor-incongruent vertical locations had a memory advantage in the reported experiments.
original.method: Four experiments varied the vertical location of positive and negative words during encoding, retrieval, or hand movements and tested recall or recognition.
original.population: University of Richmond undergraduates: 18, 34, 30, and 40 participants in the four experiments, respectively.
original.outcome_measure: Free recall and recognition memory for positive and negative words.

evidence.quote: Four experiments examined whether memory for positive and negative words depended on word location and vertical hand movements... we find a memory advantage for words that had been studied in metaphor incongruent locations
Eighteen University of Richmond undergraduates... Thirty-four University of Richmond undergraduates... Thirty University of Richmond undergraduates... Forty University of Richmond undergraduates

original.claim: Participants prompted to think about personal mortality discounted future monetary gains less than those prompted to think about dental pain.
original.method: Participants were randomly assigned to a mortality-salience or dental-pain condition and completed an intertemporal monetary-choice task.
original.population: 118 undergraduate students, 90 of them women.
original.outcome_measure: The delayed reward amount participants required instead of receiving $50 immediately.

participants in the mortality salience condition discounted future monetary gains less than other participants

original.claim: Women expecting to interact with an attractive man displayed red more often than a baseline, while those expecting an unattractive man displayed red less often.
original.method: Women received an email with a photograph of an ostensibly assigned male research assistant varying in attractiveness, then were photographed and assessed for red display.
original.population: 74 self-reported heterosexual or bisexual women retained for analysis in Germany.
original.outcome_measure: Display of red in clothing, accessories, or makeup.

original.claim: Participants associated conjunction descriptions with perceptually unified displays and disjunction descriptions with perceptually separate displays.

original.population: Three samples of 20 English-speaking participants, one for each experiment.
original.outcome_measure: Description-validation responses and response times.

original.claim: Higher intolerance of uncertainty was associated with more generalized threat responding and delayed threat-safety discrimination.
original.method: Researchers recorded skin conductance while participants completed an associative-learning task with threat and safety cues varying in perceptual similarity.

we recorded skin conductance in 54 healthy participants during an associative learning paradigm, where threat and safety cues varied in perceptual similarity.

original.claim: Bayesian model comparison favored a heterogeneous-population model of reference-game data, especially for comprehension.
original.method: Online participants completed comprehension and production reference-game tasks involving pictured objects and restricted messages.

original.claim: A hypothetical negative income shock increased discounting of monetary gains and losses in both future and past time frames.
original.method: Online participants read positive, neutral, or negative hypothetical-income narratives and completed delay-discounting tasks with two framing formats.

original.claim: Adolescents assigned to rumination-focused cognitive behavior therapy showed lower rumination and self-reported depression across the eight-week intervention.
original.method: A randomized pilot trial assigned adolescents to eight weeks of rumination-focused cognitive behavior therapy or assessment only, with symptom measures and resting-state fMRI before and after intervention.

original.claim: Eighty-eight percent of surveyed Italian research psychologists reported using at least one questionable research practice.
original.method: Members of the Italian Association of Psychology completed an online questionnaire presenting ten practices in randomized order and four questions about each practice.
original.population: 277 Italian Association of Psychology respondents, of whom 208 completed the questionnaire.
original.outcome_measure: Prevalence estimates, admission estimates, self-admissions, and defensibility judgments for ten questionable research practices.

evidence.quote: Nearly all researchers (88%) admitted using at least one of the practices, and researchers generally considered a practice possibly defensible if they admitted using it.

evidence.location: Methods — Data collection and procedure (PDF p. 3)
evidence.quote: The mailing list included 802 dues-paying AIP members for the year 2014. There were 277 respondents (24% response rate) who answered at least part of the questionnaire and 208 respondents (75% of the 277 respondents) completed it. ... The questionnaire included 10 QRPs presented in an order randomized for each participant.

Four questions were asked for each QRP. First, participants were asked to estimate the percentage of Italian research psychologists who had ever employed the QRP (prevalence estimate). ... Third, they were asked whether they had personally ever adopted this research practice ... Fourth, they were asked whether they thought that employing the QRP is defensible.

original.claim: Brief inoculation messages that explain misleading arguments or scientific consensus reduce misinformation's adverse effects on climate-change beliefs.
original.method: Representative U.S. online samples were randomly assigned to control, misinformation, consensus, inoculation, or combined-message conditions.
original.population: Representative U.S. Qualtrics samples: 714 analyzed participants in Experiment 1 and 392 in Experiment 2.
original.outcome_measure: Perceived scientific consensus and acceptance of anthropogenic global warming.

evidence.quote: This study experimentally explored the impact of misinformation about climate change and tested several pre-emptive interventions designed to reduce the influence of misinformation. ... we found that inoculating messages that (1) explain the flawed argumentation technique used in the misinformation or that (2) highlight the scientific consensus on climate change were effective in neutralizing those adverse effects of misinformation.
The final sample of participants (N = 714) were randomly allocated to one of five groups. The final sample of participants (N = 392) were randomly allocated to the four experimental conditions.

original.claim: The tested pro-vaccination corrections do not reliably reduce vaccine misinformation and can reinforce false beliefs or lower vaccination intentions.
original.method: Students completed baseline vaccine-belief measures, were randomly assigned to one of three correction formats or unrelated fact sheets, and repeated measures immediately and after seven days.
original.population: 120 university students from Edinburgh and Naples completed both waves of the study.
original.outcome_measure: Belief in an autism-vaccine link and vaccine side effects, plus intention to vaccinate a future child.

evidence.quote: Beliefs in the autism/vaccines link and in vaccines side effects, along with intention to vaccinate a future child, were evaluated both immediately after the correction intervention and after a 7-day delay ... Results show that existing strategies to correct vaccine misinformation are ineffective and often backfire.

A total of 120 participants completed the second wave. Thus, our sample for all subsequent analyses consisted of the 120 participants who completed both waves. Participants could be exposed to one of 4 experimental conditions.

original.claim: Clinical and early-treatment data can predict treatment-resistant depression before a second antidepressant trial, with early response or week-two symptom severity especially informative.
original.method: Researchers trained machine-learning models on the STAR*D cohort, cross-validated them internally, and tested them in a hold-out STAR*D sample and independent RIS-INT-93 cohort.
original.population: Adults with major depressive disorder in STAR*D and an independent RIS-INT-93 clinical cohort; the primary report gives 190 treatment-resistant and 35 non-resistant RIS-INT-93 cases but does not state one combined total.
original.outcome_measure: Treatment-resistant versus non-treatment-resistant classification based on remission or response and model area under the curve.

evidence.quote: We used features from enrollment and level 1 treatment ... to train machine learning models ... externally validated in both the STAR*D testing dataset and RIS-INT-93 independent dataset. ... the most important feature was early or initial treatment response or symptom severity at week 2.
Data from RIS-INT-93 cohort served as an independent external test dataset ... For RIS-INT-93, there were 190 TRD cases and 35 non-TRD controls.

original.claim: In Dutch sentence processing, a male continuation after a female stereotype increases reading time, whereas the reverse does not.
original.method: Dutch readers completed an eye-tracking experiment with masculine-generic pronouns and male, female, or neutral stereotype contexts followed by a gendered continuation.
original.population: 82 analyzed Dutch readers in the eye-tracking experiment; 92 were tested initially, aged 18 to 51.
original.outcome_measure: Reading/processing time for the gendered continuation and comprehension responses.

evidence.quote: In this eye-tracking experiment (N = 82) ... we tested whether the frequently used Dutch masculine generic zijn 'his' leads to a male bias. ... After introducing a female stereotype, reading about a man led to an increase in processing time. However, the reverse did not hold.
We tested a total of 92 participants (42 male) between the ages of 18 and 51 (M = 22.8 ...). The first language of all 92 participants was Dutch.

original.claim: Greater spending on video-game loot boxes was associated with more severe problem-gambling scores.
original.method: A large online survey of gamers measured spending on loot boxes and other in-game items alongside problem-gambling severity.
original.population: 7,422 adult gamers with complete analyzable survey responses.
original.outcome_measure: Loot-box spending, other in-game spending, and problem-gambling severity.

evidence.quote: A large-scale survey of gamers (n = 7,422) found evidence for a link... between the amount that gamers spent on loot boxes and the severity of their problem gambling.
This left a total of 7,422 responses... Most participants had engaged in both purchasing loot boxes and buying other in-game items with real-world money.

original.claim: Participants expected more desirable than undesirable events for an in-group character and showed the opposite pattern for an extreme out-group character.
original.method: Researchers presented four fictional characters varying in warmth and competence and asked participants for likelihood estimates of desirable and undesirable events.
original.population: 89 German-speaking Swiss university students aged 18–30.
original.outcome_measure: Likelihood estimates for 32 desirable and undesirable events for each character.

evidence.quote: respondents manifested a strong desirability bias, expecting more desirable than undesirable events for the in-group member and the reverse pattern for the extreme out-group member.
we created four fictional characters... We then asked respondents to assess the likelihood of each character experiencing a series of identical desirable and undesirable events
Eighty-Nine Swiss university students participated in this study... participants had to be German speaking university students and aged between 18 and 30 years

original.claim: An anti-bias prompt increases students' ratings of female instructors without changing ratings of male instructors.
original.method: Students in four large-enrollment classes were randomly assigned to the usual course-evaluation form or the same form with anti-bias language.
original.population: Students enrolled in four large-enrollment classes, two taught by female instructors and two by male instructors; the primary source does not report a total numeric respondent count.
original.outcome_measure: Students' ratings of the instructor, teaching effectiveness, and course on five-point evaluation questions.

evidence.quote: Students in the anti-bias language condition had significantly higher rankings of female instructors ... There were no differences between treatment groups for male instructors. The dependent variables were ratings of instructor, teaching effectiveness, and course on five-point scales.

We conduct a randomized experiment with the student evaluations of teaching in four classes with large enrollments, two taught by male instructors and two taught by female instructors. In each of the courses, students were randomly assigned to either receive the standard evaluation instrument or the same instrument with language intended to reduce gender bias.

original.claim: Action orientation partly accounted for the association between need for cognition and self-control.
original.method: A German online survey measured need for cognition, action orientation, and two self-control instruments and tested mediation and moderation models.
original.population: 1,209 survey participants, primarily young adults with university entrance diplomas.
original.outcome_measure: Self-reported self-control, need for cognition, and action orientation.

evidence.quote: Action Orientation was found to partly mediate this relation with a remaining direct effect of Need for Cognition on Self-Control.

In a sample of 1209 young adults, Self-Control was assessed with two different self-report instruments and moderation and mediation models of the relationship between Need for Cognition, Action Orientation, and Self-Control were tested.

original.claim: Visual-search distractors previously paired with high reward continue to capture attention after rewards are removed.
original.method: Undergraduates first completed a rewarded visual-search task in which distractor color signaled high or low reward, then an unrewarded test phase with the same distractor colors.
original.population: 263 undergraduate psychology students after exclusions (272 recruited).
original.outcome_measure: Visual-search response-time impairment caused by high- versus low-reward distractors.

evidence.quote: Participants initially completed a rewarded visual search task, in which colours of distractor stimuli signalled availability of high or low reward. Participants then completed a test phase in which rewards were no longer available. ... the magnitude of this reward-related distraction effect did not reduce in the subsequent unrewarded test phase.
Participants were 272 undergraduate students who completed the study as part of a first-year psychology course ... The remaining 263 participants were included in analyses.

original.claim: Identification with all humanity was a consistent predictor of cooperative health behavior and helpful responses during the COVID-19 pandemic.
original.method: A global online survey assessed identification with all humanity, four World Health Organization health behaviors, and four pandemic-related moral dilemmas.
original.population: 2,537 respondents from 87 countries and territories.
original.outcome_measure: A cooperative-health-behavior score and responses to four moral helping dilemmas.

evidence.quote: Identification with all humanity was the most consistent and consequential predictor of individuals’ cooperative health behavior and helpful responding.
we conducted a global online study (N = 2537 participants) of four WHO-recommended health behaviors and four pandemic-related moral dilemmas

original.claim: Habitually including situational cues when thinking about intended actions was positively associated with self-regulation success.
original.method: An online correlational questionnaire measured cue-inclusive thought habits, self-efficacy, self-control, and personality traits.
original.population: 392 United Kingdom adults in the full analyzed sample, aged 18–94.
original.outcome_measure: Self-reported self-efficacy, self-control beliefs, and cue-inclusive thought habits.

evidence.quote: we pre-registered and found (N = 392, age range 18–94) a positive relationship between the self-reported habitual inclusion of situational cues in thought about intended actions and everyday self-regulation success

The study is based on a correlational design with self-efficacy/control beliefs as the primary dependent variables. The primary predictor variable was the self-reported likelihood of including situational cues when thinking about intended future actions.

original.claim: After wins, players were less likely to stop and increased stakes, while after losses they started the next round more quickly.
original.method: Researchers analyzed operator-provided behavioral tracking data from an online gambling game, examining stopping, stake amount, and play speed after wins and losses.
original.population: 2,713 randomly selected players of the online game Mystery Arena.
original.outcome_measure: Whether a player stopped, stake amount, and speed of starting the next round.

evidence.quote: Using a large player-tracking data set (>2500 players, >10 million rounds)... we examined these three behavioral expressions of within-session loss-chasing.
after winning, both the high- and low-involvement groups were less likely to stop, and increased the stake amount... After losing, both groups played more quickly
In total, 2713 players were randomly selected by the operator and data on their play behavior were retrieved

original.claim: Across two surveys, greater dispositional mindfulness was associated with less pain catastrophizing and lower pain intensity and sensitivity.
original.method: Two U.S. online cross-sectional surveys measured mindfulness, pain cognitions, mood, pain intensity, and pain sensitivity and tested structural equation models.
original.population: Two U.S. adult samples of 362 and 580 participants.
original.outcome_measure: Mindfulness, pain catastrophizing, pain intensity, and pain sensitivity scores.

evidence.quote: Two independent, online cross-sectional surveys (Ns = 362 and 580 U.S. adults) were conducted. Participants completed validated assessments of mindfulness, pain catastrophizing, fear of pain, pain vigilance, depression, pain intensity, and pain sensitivity. Using structural equation modeling, we tested the inclusion of dispositional mindfulness in the fear-avoidance model of pain.
greater mindfulness was significantly associated with less pain catastrophizing and, in turn, lower levels of pain intensity and pain sensitivity.

original.claim: Untrained observers rated the speaker's communication competence higher in the post-treatment video than in the pre-treatment video.
original.method: Online observers viewed one of two mock-interview videos recorded before or after communication-centered treatment and rated the speaker on a visual analog scale.
original.population: 81 untrained online observers.
original.outcome_measure: Observer-rated communication competence on a 100-point visual analog scale.

evidence.quote: Eighty-one untrained observers completed an online survey that required each to view one of two videos depicting an adult who stutters during a mock interview recorded prior to CCT or after CCT.

Observers were then asked to rate the communication competence of the interviewee on a 100-point visual analog scale... Communication competence... was rated significantly higher in their post-treatment video.

original.claim: The shortened 12-item German ETMCQ had good model fit, whereas the proposed original structure had insufficient fit.
original.method: Two cross-sectional samples completed self-report measures that were analyzed with confirmatory factor analysis, group comparisons, correlations, and structural equation modeling.
original.population: 584 German-speaking general-population participants and a second sample of 30 clinical and 30 non-clinical participants.
original.outcome_measure: ETMCQ factor structure, clinical-group comparisons, and associations with trauma, personality, functioning, and mentalization measures.

evidence.quote: Regarding the factorial validity, the model fit of the originally proposed ETMCQ proved to be insufficient. The model fit to the data was good for a shortened 12-item version.

The aim of this study is to test the factorial, convergent, and discriminant validity of the German version of the new Epistemic Trust, Mistrust and Credulity–Questionnaire (ETMCQ). Data were collected cross-sectionally from the German-speaking general population (N = 584) and in a second sample of clinical (n = 30) and non-clinical (n = 30) participants.

evidence.location: Abstract and Methods — Study design (PDF pp. 1, 4)
evidence.quote: The previously proposed three-factor structure of the ETMCQ was analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis. The ETMCQ’s ability to differentiate between clinical and non-clinical participants was tested with t-tests. Correlations with early childhood trauma, maladaptive personality traits, and impairments in personality functioning were examined. The relationship between epistemic trust and mentalization was analyzed in a structural equation model. ... Two independent samples were recruited.

original.claim: In a remitted recurrent-depression community sample, stronger happiness valuation was associated with more depressive symptoms.
original.method: Participants completed diagnostic interviewing and an online survey of happiness valuation, depressive symptoms, neuroticism, and social desirability before any treatment assignment.
original.population: Ninety-eight Denver-area community participants currently remitted from major depressive disorder with at least three prior episodes.
original.outcome_measure: A seven-item valuing-happiness scale and the 22-item Beck Depression Inventory composite symptom score.

evidence.quote: Participants were a community sample (N = 98) recruited from the Denver metropolitan area. The Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV confirmed that participants were currently remitted from MDD and had a history of at least three prior episodes of MDD.

All relevant study measures were collected before randomization to treatment had occurred. After obtaining informed consent, the SCID-CT was administered by trained interviewers. Several days later, participants reported their demographics, valuing happiness, depression symptoms, neuroticism, and social desirability in an online survey.
Valuing happiness was correlated with increased depressive symptoms, r = .27, p = .008.

evidence.location: Study 1: Valuing Happiness and Depressive Symptoms
evidence.quote: The valuing happiness scale consists of seven items measuring to what extent participants highly value happiness. The Beck Depression Inventory consists of 22 items assessing current depressive symptoms that were summed to create a composite depressive symptom score.

original.claim: The relative duration of spontaneous alpha bursts predicted retrospective duration estimates during quiet wakefulness but not prospective duration estimates.
original.method: Right-handed participants completed quiet-wakefulness MEG recordings with retrospective timing, and a subgroup later completed prospective timing.
original.population: 56 analyzed right-handed participants in retrospective timing; 24 of 25 in the prospective-timing subgroup.
original.outcome_measure: Relative alpha-burst duration and participants’ retrospective and prospective duration estimates.

evidence.quote: When participants were not instructed to attend to time, the relative duration of α bursts linearly predicted individuals' retrospective estimates of how long their quiet wakefulness lasted. ... However, when participants timed prospectively, the relative duration of α bursts failed to predict their duration estimates.

evidence.location: Abstract and Materials and Methods — Experimental design (PMC full text)
evidence.quote: Participants stayed quietly awake for a few minutes while being recorded with magnetoencephalography (MEG). They were unaware they would be asked how long the recording lasted (retrospective time) or instructed beforehand to estimate how long it will last (prospective timing). ... In the quiet wakefulness retrospective time experiment, the experimenter provided participants with the following instructions before the MEG recording: ‘I will record your brain activity at rest.’

evidence.location: Materials and Methods — Participants (PMC full text)
evidence.quote: A total of 63 right-handed participants (27 males; age = 27 years old, ±6 years) were recruited for the first study. ... Hence, a total of 56 participants (22 males; age = 27 years old, ±6 years) were analyzed in the retrospective time task. Out of the 56 participants tested in the retrospective time task, a subgroup of 25 participants performed a prospective duration estimation task: one participant was excluded from the analysis ... yielding a final sample for the prospective group of 24 participants.

original.claim: Hearing a familiar object label increased early visual P1 responses relative to an equally informative nonverbal sound cue.
original.method: English speakers heard object names or familiar nonverbal sounds before viewing familiar animal and artifact images while electroencephalography was recorded.
original.population: Fourteen English monolingual speakers participated.
original.outcome_measure: The visual P1 event-related potential within 100 milliseconds of image onset, plus behavioral responses.

evidence.quote: An analysis of ERPs showed that the P1 was larger when people were cued by labels compared with equally informative nonverbal cues—an enhancement occurring within 100 ms of image onset.

We investigated whether visual processing of images of familiar animals and artifacts was enhanced after hearing their name compared with hearing an equally familiar and unambiguous nonverbal sound in 14 English monolingual speakers.

original.claim: For three habitual coffee drinkers, a changing-criterion program reduced daily intake from almost nine cups to under three cups at treatment end, a 69% reduction that averaged 67% at 10-month follow-up.
original.method: Each participant self-monitored and graphed daily caffeine intake while an individualized changing-criterion program set gradually lower limits, with monetary prizes for meeting criteria and deposit forfeiture for exceeding them.
original.population: Three habitual coffee drinkers participated.
original.outcome_measure: Daily cups of coffee and milligrams of caffeine consumed, recorded by participants and summarized against baseline and follow-up levels.

evidence.quote: Their coffee drinking decreased from almost nine cups per day (over 1100 mg of caffeine) during baseline to less than three cups per day (less than 343 mg) at the end of treatment or a reduction of 69%. The treatment effect was maintained during a 10-month follow-up, averaging a 67% reduction from baseline.

Three habitual coffee drinkers received individualized changing criterion programs that systematically and gradually reduced their daily caffeine intake. The coffee drinkers were required to self-monitor and plot their daily intake of caffeine. They received monetary prizes for not exceeding the treatment phase criteria and forfeited a portion of their pretreatment deposit when they did.

original.claim: Two of four low-achieving target students produced their best academic work when group rewards depended on their designated-responder performance, and that contingency produced high positive social interaction in three of four observed groups.
original.method: A learning-disabilities classroom received an individualized contingency and three group contingencies that varied whether rewards depended on the group average, a designated low-achieving student, or a randomly selected student.
original.population: Primary-grade children in a learning-disabilities classroom, including four low-achieving target students and four observed groups of children.
original.outcome_measure: Academic work of target students and systematically measured group social interaction under each contingency.

evidence.quote: An individualized contingency and three group contingencies with different responder criteria (e.g., reward based on the group average, reward based on the work of a designated, low-achieving student, or reward based on the work of a randomly selected student) were applied to the academic work of primary grade children in a learning disabilities classroom.

Two of the four low-achieving target students did their best academic work during the group contingency which focused on their performance as a designated responder. This type of contingency also produced high levels of positive social interaction in three of four groups of children observed.

original.claim: An assessment methodology using reinforcement and prompt packages was useful for matching skills targeted for young autistic children to appropriate interventions.
original.method: Researchers used multiple-baseline and reversal designs to compare an assessment package with several reinforcement procedures against one with potentially effective prompts across two or three skills per child.
original.population: Six children diagnosed with autism participated.
original.outcome_measure: Performance on curriculum tasks and the relative efficacy of assessment packages for identifying appropriate skill interventions.

evidence.quote: Results suggested that the methodology was useful for matching targeted skills to appropriate interventions.

Six children who had been diagnosed with autism participated. The relative efficacy of two assessment packages—one containing several reinforcement procedures and one containing several potentially effective prompts—was evaluated across two to three skills for each child using multiple baseline and reversal designs.

original.claim: Graduate and undergraduate course test scores were higher after interteaching than after lecture, and students correctly answered more interteaching-based than lecture-based questions on the cumulative final test.
original.method: The studies alternated interteaching and lecture conditions within a graduate course and counterbalanced those conditions across two undergraduate research-methods sections, then compared quiz and test performance.
original.population: Study 1 included 35 graduate students, mostly in a one-year special-education master's program; Study 2 used two sections of an undergraduate research-methods class.
original.outcome_measure: Short quizzes, unit tests, cumulative-final-test questions, and student preference reports following instructional conditions.

evidence.quote: In Study 2, we also alternated interteaching and lecture but counterbalanced the conditions across two sections of an undergraduate research methods class.

Quiz scores following interteaching were higher than quiz scores following lecture. Again, test scores following interteaching were higher than test scores following lecture. In addition, students correctly answered more interteaching-based questions than lecture-based questions on a cumulative final test.
Participants in Study 1 were 35 graduate students, the majority of whom were in a 1-year MA degree program in special education. We alternated lecture and interteaching across class sessions.

original.claim: Repeated penile-plethysmograph assessments of ten developmentally disabled sex offenders yielded three patterns: differentiated arousal to specific inappropriate stimuli, nonspecific inappropriate-stimulus arousal, or no inappropriate-stimulus arousal with appropriate-stimulus arousal.
original.method: Researchers repeatedly measured changes in penile circumference with a penile plethysmograph while participants encountered categories of appropriate and inappropriate stimuli, using single-subject experimental assessment.
original.population: Ten individuals in a state residential treatment facility for developmentally disabled offenders were included; all had been accused of one or more sexual offenses and found incompetent to stand trial.
original.outcome_measure: Change in penile circumference during exposure to categories of appropriate and inappropriate stimuli.

evidence.quote: Overall, three general patterns of results emerged. Some participants showed differentiated deviant arousal or higher levels of arousal to specific inappropriate stimuli. Other participants showed undifferentiated deviant arousal, in which case they showed nonspecific arousal to inappropriate stimuli. The remaining participants showed no arousal to inappropriate stimuli but did show arousal to appropriate stimuli.

The arousal assessments involved measuring an individual's arousal to various types of stimuli through the use of the penile plethysmograph. A change in penile circumference is taken as an indication of an individual's arousal and is measured in the presence of different stimuli considered to be both appropriate and inappropriate.

The data from 10 individuals in a state residential treatment facility for developmentally disabled offenders were included in the current study. All of these individuals had been accused of committing one or more sexual offenses and had been found incompetent to stand trial.

original.claim: Across behavioral programs for six autistic children, discontinuous first-trial measurement was typically associated with quicker skill acquisition when measurement methods differed, whereas continuous trial-by-trial measurement was typically associated with stronger maintenance.
original.method: Six children were taught multiple skills in up to four behavioral programs, with half measured continuously on every trial and half discontinuously on the first trial only.
original.population: Six children with autism spectrum disorders aged 4 to 8 years participated.
original.outcome_measure: Skill acquisition and maintenance in discrete-trial behavioral programs under continuous versus first-trial-only recording.

evidence.quote: Six children were taught multiple skills in up to four different behavioral programs. Half of the skills were measured continuously (i.e., trial by trial), and the other half were measured discontinuously (i.e., first trial only). When differences were detected, quicker acquisition was typically associated with discontinuous measurement, and stronger maintenance was typically associated with continuous measurement.

Six children with autism spectrum disorders participated in this study. Erin was 8 years old, Jeff was 5 years old, Patrick was 7 years old, Peter was 5 years old, Mary was 4 years old, and Allison was 6 years old.

original.claim: Three children with autism acquired abduction-prevention responses after behavioral-skills training with in-situ feedback, maintained the skills at one month, and one generalized them in a community probe.
original.method: Researchers taught children to refuse a stranger's lure, leave to safety, and report to an adult through behavioral-skills training with in-situ feedback, using repeated probes before and after training.
original.population: Three boys with autism aged 6, 7, and 8 years attended the same center-based behavioral-intervention program.
original.outcome_measure: Numerically scored abduction-prevention responses to confederate stranger lures, ranging from agreeing to leave to refusing, leaving, and reporting.

evidence.quote: Three children with autism were taught abduction-prevention skills using behavioral skills training with in situ feedback. All children acquired the skills, which were maintained at a 1-month follow-up assessment. In addition, 1 of the children demonstrated the skills during a stimulus generalization probe in a community setting.

Three boys who had been diagnosed with autism served as participants. Sammy (8 years old), Michael (7 years old), and Charles (6 years old) each had extensive imitative, mand, tact, intraverbal, and instruction-following repertoires.

We taught participants the following abduction-prevention responses: saying no when presented with an abduction lure by a stranger, immediately leaving and running to a safe area, and immediately reporting the event to a familiar adult. Multiple probes were conducted before and after training to assess the effects of BST and in situ feedback.

original.claim: Eleven inexperienced school staff members showed low accuracy with written instructions alone but accurately implemented two stimulus-preference assessment methods after receiving enhanced, antecedent-only self-instructional materials.
original.method: A multiple-baseline design compared written instructions alone with enhanced written instructions that minimized technical jargon and added pictures, diagrams, and step-by-step examples for two preference-assessment methods.
original.population: Eleven teachers at a school for people with autism and related developmental disabilities, all without prior experience observing or conducting stimulus-preference assessments.
original.outcome_measure: Accuracy of staff implementation of two stimulus-preference assessment methods during simulated and generalization assessment trials.

evidence.quote: Accuracy was low when participants had access to written instructions alone. When access to enhanced written instructions was provided (i.e., technical jargon was minimized; instructions included pictures, diagrams, and step-by-step examples), inexperienced staff accurately implemented the assessments.
We used multiple baseline designs to evaluate the efficacy of an antecedent-only self-instructional package to train staff members to implement two methods of stimulus preference assessments.

Participants were 11 teachers who worked at a school for individuals with autism and related developmental disabilities. All teachers held a bachelor's degree or a master's degree and did not have previous experience observing or conducting stimulus preference assessments.

original.claim: Trust in science and COVID-19 risk perception independently predicted compliance with COVID-19 prevention guidelines.
original.method: An online survey tested a multivariate structural-equation model using demographic, ideological, psychological, risk-perception, trust, and compliance measures.
original.population: 617 survey participants.
original.outcome_measure: Self-reported compliance with COVID-19 prevention guidelines.

evidence.quote: A total of 617 participants took part in the online survey and answered several questions related to socio-demographic variables, political conservatism, religious orthodoxy, conspiracy ideation, intellectual curiosity, trust in science, COVID-19 risk perception and compliance with COVID-19 prevention guidelines.
The results of structural equation modelling (SEM) show that COVID-19 risk perception and trust in science both independently predict compliance with COVID-19 prevention guidelines

original.claim: Fear of COVID-19 predicted self-reported positive behavior change during the pandemic.
original.method: An international community survey measured perceived infection risk, fear, moral foundations, political orientation, and behavior change.
original.population: 324 participants in an international community sample.
original.outcome_measure: Self-reported behavior change, including social distancing and improved hand hygiene.

evidence.quote: Consistently, the only predictor of positive behavior change (e.g., social distancing, improved hand hygiene) was fear of COVID-19

In this study we recruited a large international community sample (N = 324) to complete measures of self-perceived risk of contracting COVID-19, fear of the virus, moral foundations, political orientation, and behavior change in response to the pandemic.

original.claim: In adolescent participants, BDNF Val66Met and a combined BDNF/5-HTTLPR score were associated with rumination and co-rumination measures.
original.method: Two community youth studies collected genotype data and questionnaire measures of rumination, co-rumination, and depressive symptoms.
original.population: 228 youth with complete data in Study I and 87 youth in Study II, ages 8–14 at recruitment.
original.outcome_measure: Rumination and co-rumination questionnaire scores.

evidence.quote: In Study I, 228 youth (ages 8–14)... were recruited from the community... Study II, a sample of 87 youth... In Study I, the Val66Met... polymorphism was associated with rumination in adolescents... [and] a cumulative genetic score... predicted higher levels of co-rumination
Study I analyses were based on 228 youth with complete assessment and genetic data... Youth’s participation was limited such that no more than one child per mother could participate

original.claim: Participants who had experienced COVID-19 showed a pattern of memory deficits that increased with the severity of self-reported ongoing symptoms.
original.method: Researchers assessed memory, language, and executive function in a COVID-experienced group and a non-COVID comparison group.
original.population: 181 people who had experienced COVID-19 and 185 who had not.
original.outcome_measure: Performance on memory, language, and executive-function tests.

evidence.quote: In this second paper from the study, we assess this sample on tests of memory, language, and executive function... We found a consistent pattern of memory deficits in those that had experienced the COVID-19 infection, with deficits increasing with the severity of self-reported ongoing symptoms.
The first paper from the study explored the characteristics of our sample of 181 individuals who had experienced the COVID-19 infection, and 185 who had not.

original.claim: Choosing to deceive in a strategic sender-receiver game was associated with activity in a temporo-parietal, cingulate, precuneus, and anterior-frontal network.
original.method: Right-handed adults completed an fMRI sender-receiver game in which they could send truthful or deceptive payoff messages.
original.population: 34 healthy German-speaking adults; five were excluded from analysis for too few trials in key choice categories.
original.outcome_measure: BOLD activity during deceptive and truthful message choices.

evidence.quote: Using a game-theoretic setting, we investigate the neural basis of deception in human interaction... We find activation within the right temporo-parietal junction... dorsal anterior cingulate cortex... (pre)cuneus, and the anterior frontal gyrus when contrasting lying with truth telling.
Thirty-four... healthy volunteers... participated in the fMRI experiment... In the sender-receiver game... the sender... can send either of two messages

original.claim: Extraversion was positively associated with the normalized clustering coefficient of resting-state brain networks.
original.method: Researchers measured resting-state functional connectivity across 90 brain regions and applied graph-theoretical analysis.
original.population: 71 healthy subjects with usable resting-state fMRI data.
original.outcome_measure: Normalized clustering coefficient of whole-brain functional networks.

evidence.quote: Graph theoretical analysis revealed a positive association of extraversion scores and normalized clustering coefficient values.

To construct functional brain networks, functional connectivity among 90 brain regions was measured by temporal correlation using resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data of 71 healthy subjects.

original.claim: The Landolt reading condition engaged a visual-scanning network while separating it from semantic, syntactic, and orthographic processing regions.
original.method: Healthy volunteers underwent fMRI while reading words, pseudowords, sentences, lists, and a Landolt-ring scanning condition.
original.population: 20 healthy adults aged 20–30 years.
original.outcome_measure: fMRI activation across reading and gaze-orienting conditions.

evidence.quote: Here, 20 healthy volunteers underwent fMRI scanning while reading sentences... lists... words... pseudowords... In an additional ‘Landolt reading’ condition, all letters were replaced by closed circles... A conjunction analysis... revealed the visual scanning network

original.claim: Children with developmental dyslexia showed a different preferred delta-band phase of neural entrainment to rhythmic speech than control children.
original.method: Children with and without dyslexia completed an EEG task using rhythmic auditory, visual, and audiovisual syllable streams and a delay-detection response.
original.population: 21 typically developing children and 11 children with developmental dyslexia.
original.outcome_measure: EEG entrainment phase and cross-correlation measures of neural stimulus representation.

evidence.quote: A rhythmic paradigm... was used to study... oscillatory entrainment to speech in children with and without dyslexia using EEG... The data showed a significant group difference in the preferred phase of entrainment in the delta band
We studied 21 typically-developing children and 11 children with a history of developmental dyslexia

original.claim: High-frequency variants in the ME/CFS cohort were functionally concentrated in immune, hormone, metabolic, and extracellular-matrix pathways.
original.method: Researchers filtered 23andMe genome-wide SNP data from ME/CFS participants, compared variant frequencies with a reference database, and performed pathway analysis.
original.population: 383 participants with myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome.
original.outcome_measure: Frequency and functional-pathway annotation of SNPs.

evidence.quote: 383 ME/CFS participants underwent DNA testing using the commercial company 23andMe. The deidentified genetic data was then filtered... The frequencies of each SNP were calculated within our cohort and compared to frequencies from the Kaviar reference database. Functional annotation... was performed
Functional analysis identified the majority of SNPs as related to immune system, hormone, metabolic, and extracellular matrix organization.

original.claim: Women scored higher on several Big Five aspects including Enthusiasm, Compassion, Politeness, Volatility, Withdrawal, and Openness, while men scored higher on Assertiveness and Intellect.
original.method: Researchers administered Big Five Aspect Scales and compared aspect scores by gender.
original.population: 2,643 participants aged 17–85 from Canadian, U.S. community, and online samples.
