Participants rate their agreement with how well each statement describes them using a five-point scale... Scores for each aspect are computed by taking the mean of the corresponding items.
Women scored higher than men on Enthusiasm, Compassion, Politeness, Orderliness, Volatility, Withdrawal, and Openness. Men scored higher than women on Assertiveness and Intellect.

original.claim: More frequent everyday language switching was related to a smaller mixing cost in errors on the set-shifting task.
original.method: Finnish–Swedish bilinguals completed a language-switching questionnaire and executive-function tasks, and the associations were assessed with multiple regression.
original.population: 38 Finnish–Swedish bilingual adults aged 30–75 years.
original.outcome_measure: Performance measures of inhibition, updating, and set shifting, including mixing cost in errors.

evidence.quote: Most consistent effects were found for the set shifting task where a higher rate of everyday language switches was related to a smaller mixing cost in errors.

We employed multiple regression to study whether the performance of 30- to 75-year-old Finnish–Swedish bilinguals (N = 38) on tasks measuring different executive functions (inhibition, updating, and set shifting) could be predicted by the frequency of language switches in everyday life (as measured by a language switching questionnaire), L2 age of acquisition, or by the self-estimated degree of use of both languages in everyday life.

Multiple linear regression analyses were conducted for the processing cost in RTs and error rates, separately for each executive task. ... The second group of predictors included three measures from the BSWQ: the BSWQ language switching measure, the BSWQ contextual switches measure, and the BSWQ unintended switches measure.

original.claim: The implicit-association task did not show support for Kandinsky's proposed color-shape combinations.
original.method: Participants completed three implicit-association tasks classifying color and shape stimuli with congruent or incongruent key mappings.
original.population: 36 participants aged 18–45.
original.outcome_measure: Response times under congruent and incongruent color-shape key mappings.

evidence.quote: Participants pressed one of two buttons on each trial. On some trials they classified shapes... On interleaved trials they classified colors... Our findings suggest that there is no implicit association between the original color-form combinations.
Thirty-six participants were involved (age 18–45, 11 male, 6 left handed).

original.claim: Habit strength statistically accounted for the association between trait self-control and unhealthy snack intake.
original.method: University students completed measures of trait self-control and snacking habits and kept a seven-day food diary.
original.population: 77 Dutch university students, predominantly women.
original.outcome_measure: Trait self-control, habit strength, and unhealthy snack consumption.

evidence.quote: Results showed that self-control was negatively associated with unhealthy snack consumption and unhealthy snacking habits. As hypothesized, the relation between self-control and unhealthy snack intake was mediated by habit strength.
participants were asked to fill out an online questionnaire on self-control, snacking habits, and unhealthy snack consumption... the final sample consisted of 77 participants.

original.claim: Accurate breath counting is a behavioral measure of mindfulness and is associated with less mind wandering.
original.method: Across four independent studies, participants completed a breath-counting task and related self-report or cognitive measures; one study randomly assigned online training for four weeks.
original.population: More than 400 participants across four independent studies.
original.outcome_measure: Breath-counting accuracy, self-reported mindfulness, mind wandering, mood, and non-attachment.

evidence.quote: In four independent studies with over 400 total participants, we present the first construct validation of a behavioral measure of mindfulness, breath counting. We found it was reliable, correlated with self-reported mindfulness ... As theorized, we found skill in breath counting associated with more meta-awareness, less mind wandering, better mood, and greater non-attachment.

We also found in a randomized online training study that 4 weeks of breath counting training improved mindfulness and decreased mind wandering relative to working memory training and no training controls.

original.claim: Cleanliness priming reduced the severity of moral judgments under low-response-effort instructions, but not under high-response-effort instructions.
original.method: Online U.S. adults completed a sentence-unscrambling priming task under low- or high-response-effort instructions before rating moral vignettes.
original.population: 440 analyzed English-speaking U.S. adults recruited through Mechanical Turk in Study 2.
original.outcome_measure: Composite and individual-vignette moral-judgment ratings.

evidence.quote: Support for the cleanliness hypothesis was found among participants instructed to work through the sentence unscrambling task as quickly as possible. In contrast, when participants were instructed to work on the sentence unscrambling task attentively, no support was found for the hypothesized effect of the cleanliness priming.

evidence.location: Study 2 — Materials and Method (PDF p. 5) and Table 2 (PDF p. 6)
evidence.quote: The survey measures in the current study were identical to those in Study 1. The moral judgment composite had an internal consistency reliability of 0.65. ... Mean ratings for moral vignettes in study 2. Condition Composite rating Individual vignette rating.

Five hundred and thirty-five English-speaking adults residing in the United States ... recruited from Mturk completed this online survey ... Of these, 440 ... were retained in the analysis after planned exclusion. ... Participants were randomly assigned into one of two response effort instructional sets for the sentence unscrambling task. Those in the low response effort condition ... read ‘Work as quickly as you can.’ In contrast, those in the high response effort condition ... read ‘Work quickly ... but perform to the best of your ability.’

original.claim: The number of lifetime perpetrated violent acts predicted appetitive aggression, whereas it did not predict posttraumatic-stress symptoms.
original.method: Researchers interviewed former armed-group members about combat exposure, trauma symptoms, aggression, depression, suicidality, and drug dependence.
original.population: 213 former members of armed groups in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
original.outcome_measure: Appetitive-aggression and posttraumatic-stress symptom measures.

evidence.quote: the number of lifetime perpetrated violent acts was the most important predictor of appetitive aggression. However, the number of perpetrated violent acts did not significantly affect the posttraumatic stress.

we interviewed 213 former members of (para)military groups in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo in regard to their combat exposure, posttraumatic stress, appetitive aggression, depression, suicidality, and drug dependence.

original.claim: Psychological well-being was associated with emotional fit in the culturally central life domain in each of the three samples.
original.method: Participants described autonomy- or relatedness-promoting situations, rated their emotions, and researchers compared individual emotion patterns with cultural-average patterns.
original.population: 30 European Americans, 80 Koreans, and 266 Belgians.
original.outcome_measure: Emotional fit with the cultural pattern and psychological well-being.

evidence.quote: We tested this hypothesis with samples from three cultural contexts... a European American (N = 30), a Korean (N = 80), and a Belgian sample (N = 266). Cultural fit was measured by comparing an individual's patterns of emotions to the average cultural pattern for the same type of situation.
in each sample, psychological well-being was associated with emotional fit in the domain that was key to the cultural mandate.

original.claim: Greater interoceptive sensitivity was associated with less distress and affiliation response to social exclusion.
original.method: One study used a Cyberball social-exclusion task and another assessed habitual emotion-regulation strategies alongside interoceptive sensitivity.
original.population: 69 female participants in the Cyberball study and 116 participants in the emotion-regulation study.
original.outcome_measure: Distress, behavioral affiliation tendencies, interoceptive sensitivity, and emotion-regulation strategies.

evidence.quote: The first study investigated subjective feelings and behavioral affiliation tendencies in response to ostracism using a cyberball paradigm. Sixty-nine participants were assessed... The second study examined habitual emotion regulation processes... in 116 participants.
being ostracized had less impact on participants with stronger IS.

original.claim: Students made more correct Bayesian inferences with natural-frequency information than with probability information.
original.method: Students solved medical and economic Bayesian-reasoning tasks that varied visualization format and whether information was presented as probabilities or natural frequencies.
original.population: 259 German secondary-school students aged 16–18.
original.outcome_measure: Correct Bayesian inferences on the mammography and economics problems.

evidence.quote: Each of N = 259 participants (students of age 16–18) had to solve two typical Bayesian reasoning tasks (‘mammography problem’ and ‘economics problem’).
students’ performance was higher when information in the problems was presented in natural frequencies (42% correct inferences... ) instead of probabilities (5%).

original.claim: Athletes assigned to the ego-depletion condition showed an increase in false starts from before to after the manipulation, unlike the comparison group.
original.method: Female soccer players completed sprint-start trials before and after a depletion or non-depletion task in a mixed design.
original.population: 38 collegiate female soccer players without track-and-field experience.
original.outcome_measure: Number of false starts at the two sprint-start assessments.

evidence.quote: in a sample of N = 38 athletes without track and field experience... there was only a significant increase in the number of false starts from T1 to T2 for the depletion group while this was not the case for the non-depletion group.
Our sample consisted of 38 Collegiate level female soccer players... Participants were randomly assigned to a depletion group... or a non-depletion group

original.claim: Repeated pseudowords and consonant strings were judged as shorter in duration than novel comparison stimuli.
original.method: Two within-subject experiments presented a standard and comparison stimulus, varying repetition and inter-stimulus interval before a duration judgment.
original.population: 32 volunteers in each experiment.
original.outcome_measure: Judgments of whether the comparison stimulus was shorter or longer than the standard.

evidence.quote: Two experiments investigated the effects of stimulus repetition vs. stimulus novelty on perceived duration... In both experiments, we observed shorter judged durations for repeated than for novel comparisons.
The data of 32 volunteers... entered the analyses... A fresh sample of 32 volunteers... participated in the experiment.

original.claim: Black evaluators gave Black employment candidates with Afrocentric hair higher dominance ratings and lower professionalism ratings than candidates with Eurocentric hair.
original.method: Three online experiments manipulated target hairstyle and examined evaluator race in ratings of Black women employment candidates.
original.population: 200 participants in Study 1, 510 in Study 2, and 291 in Study 3.
original.outcome_measure: Ratings of candidates' professionalism and dominance.

We conducted three experimental studies to examine the influence of target hairstyle and participant race on ratings of the target’s professionalism... and dominance... Study 1... 200 participants... Study 2... 510 participants... Study 3... 291 participants.

original.claim: Sluices with garden-path antecedents had shorter processing times than sluices with non-garden-path antecedents.
original.method: Native German speakers completed a moving-window self-paced-reading experiment with sluicing sentences and comprehension questions.
original.population: 60 University of Potsdam students who were native German speakers.
original.outcome_measure: Self-paced reading times and comprehension-task responses.

evidence.quote: In a self-paced reading experiment, we investigated the processing of sluicing constructions... Results showed decreased processing times for sluices with garden-path antecedents
Sixty students from the University of Potsdam were recruited for the study. All subjects were native speakers of German

original.claim: Religious music's association with dishonest reporting differed across sites and varied with participant religiosity.
original.method: Participants in Mauritius, the Czech Republic, and the United States heard religious music, secular music, or white noise before a paid matrix-solving task with self-reported performance.
original.population: 254 participants across Mauritian, Czech, and U.S. sites.
original.outcome_measure: Self-reported number of correctly solved mathematical matrices and religiosity.

evidence.quote: Participants were exposed to one of three kinds of auditory stimuli (religious, secular, or white noise), and subsequently were given a chance to dishonestly report on solved mathematical equations in order to increase their monetary reward.
The results showed cross-cultural differences in the effects of religious music on moral behavior, as well as a significant interaction between condition and religiosity across all sites.
Across the three sites, 254 participants were randomly assigned to one of three conditions: religious, secular, and control.

original.claim: Adults learned contextual meanings in an artificial language when the context was socially salient, coherent, and interpretable.
original.method: Online artificial-language games trained adults on contextual meanings of a word-formation pattern and tested generalization to new forms and contexts.
original.population: Separate U.S. Amazon Mechanical Turk samples across four experiments; the first experiment retained 45 participants.
original.outcome_measure: Learning and generalization of contextual meanings for an artificial-language pattern.

evidence.quote: Through a series of short games, played online, we test how well adults can learn different contextual meanings for a word-formation pattern in an artificial language... The experiment was hosted on Amazon Mechanical Turk... 47 people participated... we removed 2 participants and report data from 45 participants.

original.claim: Contingent changes in a line-drawn face increased ultimatum-game offers in robot and teleoperation settings.
original.method: Two experiments had student participants act as proposers in an ultimatum game while viewing a contingent or static line-drawn face.
original.population: 26 healthy graduate and undergraduate students in Study 1; a second student sample completed Study 2.
original.outcome_measure: Ultimatum-game offer amount.

Twenty-six healthy graduate and undergraduate students... participated in the experiment.

original.claim: Need for cognition predicts university-study satisfaction and indirectly predicts fewer thoughts of changing or quitting a major.
original.method: German university students completed an online survey of need for cognition, academic performance, satisfaction, and termination thoughts; correlations and path analysis were used.
original.population: 396 students from different subjects at a German university; mean age 24 years.
original.outcome_measure: Need for Cognition, school performance, study satisfaction, and thoughts of quitting or changing major.

evidence.quote: All participants took part in an online survey that assessed NFC together with school performance and further personality variables via self-report.

The current sample consisted of 396 students ... Success in university was comprehensively operationalized including performance, satisfaction with one’s studies, and thoughts about quitting/changing one’s major ... Path analysis confirmed the importance of NFC for study satisfaction.

original.claim: Pluralistic ignorance about paternity leave is associated with Japanese men's weaker intentions to take leave.
original.method: Two survey studies measured male employees' own beliefs, beliefs about other men's views, and intentions to take paternity leave.
original.population: Japanese male employees: 299 in Study 1 and 425 in Study 2.
original.outcome_measure: Beliefs about paternity leave and intention to take paternity leave.

evidence.quote: Study 1 (n = 299) examined Japanese male employees’ ... Study 2 (n = 425) ... Together, our findings suggest that pluralistic ignorance inhibits Japanese male employees’ intentions to take paternity leave.
The current research examined the association between beliefs about gender-role norms, perceived beliefs of others, and intentions to take paternity leave.

original.claim: Panic-disorder severity and work participation improved after the four-day treatment in the pilot sample.
original.method: Consecutively referred patients with panic disorder completed the Bergen four-day treatment and structured symptom assessments before and after treatment.
original.population: 29 Norwegian patients with panic disorder, 21 with agoraphobia.
original.outcome_measure: Panic Disorder Severity Scale, reliable change, remission, and work participation.

patients... who fulfilled the diagnostic criteria of PD with or without agoraphobia were offered participation in the 4-day treatment... Twenty-nine patients were given a diagnosis of PD

original.claim: Objectively assessed cognitive inflexibility predicted endorsement of violence for the national group and willingness to die for the group.
original.method: United Kingdom and United States online samples completed cognitive tasks and questionnaires about national-group attitudes, violence endorsement, and self-sacrifice.
original.population: Two United Kingdom and United States samples totaling 1,047 participants.
original.outcome_measure: Cognitive flexibility-task performance, endorsement of violence, and willingness to die for the group.

evidence.quote: Participants... completed the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test and cognitive tasks... Participants were asked about demographic variables and ideological attitudes

original.claim: Only about one fifth of surveyed participants support paying for social-media apps in exchange for greater privacy and fewer social-media problems.
original.method: A convenience sample completed questionnaires about willingness to pay for private social-media or messenger services and personality traits.
original.population: 210 participants: 117 male, 91 female, and 2 third gender.
original.outcome_measure: Support for a payment model, stated willingness to pay, and personality measures.

The sample comprised N = 210 participants (n = 117 males; n = 91 females; n = 2 'third gender').

original.claim: Chinese students recalled more guilt- and shame-related self-defining memories than American students.
original.method: Chinese and American college students wrote and rated two self-defining memories, completed memory-function and personality questionnaires, and had memory content coded.

original.outcome_measure: Memory affect, frequency, importance, content coding, memory function, and Big Five scores.

evidence.quote: It examined SDMs, Big Five personality traits, and memory function in 60 students from each country (n = 120). Participants rated their memories for affect, recall frequency, and importance... Chinese students recalled significantly more guilt/shame events than American students.
participants in both countries filled out the same battery of questionnaires... SDM Request, Memory Rating Scales, TALE, The BFI-10, and Demographics.

original.claim: Respondents reported higher attribution of consciousness to living and non-living entities after a belief-changing psychedelic experience than before it.
original.method: An online survey asked respondents with a belief-changing psychedelic experience to rate consciousness attribution and related beliefs before and after that experience.
original.population: 1,606 respondents with a self-reported belief-changing psychedelic experience.
original.outcome_measure: Ratings of consciousness attribution, superstitious beliefs, freewill beliefs, and mystical experience.

From before the experience to after, there were large increases in attribution of consciousness to various entities

original.claim: Senior police officers receiving the intervention training improved response time and time to first hit in shoot/don't-shoot scenarios.
original.method: A preregistered laboratory experiment randomly assigned police officers to video-based situational-awareness and gaze-control training or active conventional training before pre- and post-tests.
original.population: 45 senior police officers in Germany.
original.outcome_measure: Decision-making, muzzle position, tactical conduct, response time, and time to first hit in realistic scenarios.

the intervention group significantly improved their response times and time until the first hit.

original.method: Police cadets were randomly assigned to the video-based intervention or an active traditional-marksmanship control and completed pre- and post-tests using dynamic scenarios.

N = 52 second-year police cadets... volunteered for the study.

original.claim: Five self-regulated-learning profiles emerged, and higher-competency profiles showed better learning success and more favorable goal orientations than lower-competency profiles.

original.claim: Frontal-eye-field stimulation changes saccade latency and reduces erroneous reflexive saccades in antisaccade tasks.

Sixteen subjects (6 males and 10 females) were recruited ... subjects in each of our experiment (n = 16 for each experiment).

original.claim: The two patient groups reported more sleep problems and lower sleep quality than healthy controls.
